cues.zh: 我认为算力将成为未来的货币。
cues.en: I think compute is going to be the currency of the future.

cues.zh: 我认为它可能会是世界上最有价值的东西。
cues.en: I think it’ll be maybe the most precious commodity in the world.

cues.zh: 我预计到这个十年结束时，可能还会更早一些，我们将拥有相当强大的系统，我们会看着它说：“哇，这真是太了不起了。”通往AGI的道路应该是一场巨大的权力斗争。
cues.en: I expect that by the end of this decade, and possibly somewhat sooner than that, we will have quite capable systems that we look at and say, “Wow, that’s really remarkable.” The road to AGI should be a giant power struggle.

cues.zh: 我预计会是这样。
cues.en: I expect that to be the case.

cues.zh: 谁先造出AGI，谁就能获得巨大的权力。
cues.en: Whoever builds AGI first gets a lot of power.

cues.zh: 你信任自己能掌握那么大的权力吗？
cues.en: Do you trust yourself with that much power?

cues.zh: 以下是与Sam Altman的对话，这是他第二次做客播客。
cues.en: The following is a conversation with Sam Altman, his second time on the podcast.

cues.zh: 他是OpenAI的CEO，这家公司打造了GPT-4、ChatGPT、Sora，也许有一天，正是这家公司将造出AGI。
cues.en: He is the CEO of OpenAI, the company behind GPT-4, ChaTGPT, Sora, and perhaps one day the very company that will build AGI.

cues.zh: 这里是Lex Fridman播客。
cues.en: This is The Lex Fridman Podcast.

cues.zh: 想支持我们，请查看简介中的赞助商。
cues.en: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

cues.zh: 接下来，亲爱的朋友们，有请Sam Altman。
cues.en: And now, dear friends, here’s Sam Altman.

cues.zh: 带我回顾一下从11月16日周四，也许对你来说是11月17日周五开始的OpenAI董事会风波吧。
cues.en: Take me through the OpenAI board saga that started on Thursday, November 16th, maybe Friday, November 17th for you.

cues.zh: 那绝对是我人生中最痛苦的职业经历，混乱、羞耻、令人不安，还有一堆其他负面的事。
cues.en: That was definitely the most painful professional experience of my life, and chaotic and shameful and upsetting and a bunch of other negative things.

cues.zh: 其中也有好的方面，我真希望当时不是那么肾上腺素飙升，让我没能停下来好好体会它们。
cues.en: There were great things about it too, and I wish it had not been in such an adrenaline rush that I wasn’t able to stop and appreciate them at the time.

cues.zh: 但我翻到了我以前的这条推文，或者说那个时期我发的这条推文。
cues.en: But I came across this old tweet of mine or this tweet of mine from that time period.

cues.zh: 那感觉就像在听自己的悼词，看着人们说你的各种好话，还有来自我爱的人和在乎的人难以置信的支持。
cues.en: It was like going your own eulogy, watching people say all these great things about you, and just unbelievable support from people I love and care about.

cues.zh: 那真的很暖心，真的很暖心。
cues.en: That was really nice, really nice.

cues.zh: 那个周末整体上，除了一个很大的例外，我感受到很多爱，很少恨，尽管当时感觉完全不知道这里正在发生什么、接下来会发生什么，这种感觉真的很糟。
cues.en: That whole weekend, with one big exception, I felt like a great deal of love and very little hate, even though it felt like I have no idea what’s happening and what’s going to happen here and this feels really bad.

cues.zh: 确实有些时刻，我觉得这可能会成为对 AI 安全来说最糟糕的事情之一。
cues.en: And there were definitely times I thought it was going to be one of the worst things to ever happen for AI safety.

cues.zh: 不过，我也觉得挺庆幸这事发生得相对较早。
cues.en: Well, I also think I’m happy that it happened relatively early.

cues.zh: 我原以为在 OpenAI 成立到我们创造出 AGI 之间的某个时刻，会发生某种疯狂而爆炸性的事情，但也许还有更多疯狂和爆炸性的事情尚未发生。
cues.en: I thought at some point between when OpenAI started and when we created AGI, there was going to be something crazy and explosive that happened, but there may be more crazy and explosive things still to happen.

cues.zh: 我认为它仍然帮助我们建立了一些韧性，为未来的更多挑战做好准备。
cues.en: It still, I think, helped us build up some resilience and be ready for more challenges in the future.

cues.zh: 但你当时有种感觉，觉得会经历某种权力斗争？
cues.en: But the thing you had a sense that you would experience is some kind of power struggle?

cues.zh: 通往 AGI 的道路应该是一场巨大的权力斗争。
cues.en: The road to AGI should be a giant power struggle.

cues.zh: 世界应该……好吧，不是应该。
cues.en: The world should… Well, not should.

cues.zh: 我预计情况会是这样。
cues.en: I expect that to be the case.

cues.zh: 所以你必须经历这些，就像你说的，尽可能频繁地迭代，去弄清楚如何建立董事会结构、如何组织公司、如何选择共事的人、如何沟通这一切，从而尽可能缓和权力斗争。
cues.en: And so you have to go through that, like you said, iterate as often as possible in figuring out how to have a board structure, how to have organization, how to have the kind of people that you’re working with, how to communicate all that in order to deescalate the power struggle as much as possible.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 安抚它。
cues.en: Pacify it.

cues.zh: 但现在，感觉那像是过去的事了，当时真的非常不愉快、非常艰难和痛苦，不过我们已回归工作，事情又忙又紧张，我没花太多时间去想它。
cues.en: But at this point, it feels like something that was in the past that was really unpleasant and really difficult and painful, but we’re back to work and things are so busy and so intense that I don’t spend a lot of time thinking about it.

cues.zh: 那之后有一段时间，大概是一个月，也许45天吧，我整个人处于一种恍惚状态，每天就是浑浑噩噩地过日子。
cues.en: There was a time after, there was this fugue state for the month after, maybe 45 days after, that I was just drifting through the days.

cues.zh: 我完全不在状态。
cues.en: I was so out of it.

cues.zh: 我情绪特别低落。
cues.en: I was feeling so down.

cues.zh: 就个人心理层面来说？
cues.en: Just on a personal, psychological level?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 真的非常痛苦，而且在那期间还得继续运营OpenAI，特别难熬。
cues.en: Really painful, and hard to have to keep running OpenAI in the middle of that.

cues.zh: 我只想躲进一个洞穴里，好好恢复一阵子。
cues.en: I just wanted to crawl into a cave and recover for a while.

cues.zh: 但现在我们算是回到正轨，继续推进使命了。
cues.en: But now it’s like we’re just back to working on the mission.

cues.zh: 不过回头去看那段经历还是有用的，反思董事会结构、权力动态、公司怎么运作，以及研究、产品开发、资金这些东西之间的张力，这样你们这些极有可能造出AGI的人，未来能以更有条理、少些戏剧性的方式去做这件事。
cues.en: Well, it’s still useful to go back there and reflect on board structures, on power dynamics, on how companies are run, the tension between research and product development and money and all this kind of stuff so that you, who have a very high potential of building AGI, would do so in a slightly more organized, less dramatic way in the future.

cues.zh: 所以这方面确实有价值，既包括你作为领导者的个人心理层面，也包括董事会结构以及所有这些复杂的事情。
cues.en: So there’s value there to go, both the personal psychological aspects of you as a leader, and also just the board structure and all this messy stuff.

cues.zh: 我确实学到了很多关于结构、激励机制，以及我们需要董事会提供什么。
cues.en: I definitely learned a lot about structure and incentives and what we need out of a board.

cues.zh: 而且我觉得，从某种意义上说，这件事现在发生是有价值的。
cues.en: And I think that it is valuable that this happened now in some sense.

cues.zh: 我认为这大概不是 OpenAI 最后一次高压时刻，但这次确实是相当高压的时刻。
cues.en: I think this is probably not the last high-stress moment of OpenAI, but it was quite a high-stress moment.

cues.zh: 我的公司差点就被毁了。
cues.en: My company very nearly got destroyed.

cues.zh: 我们会花很多精力思考，为了 AGI 还有很多其他事情必须做对，但思考如何建立一个有韧性的组织、如何建立一个能承受世界上大量压力的结构——随着我们越来越接近，我预计这种压力会越来越多——我觉得这超级重要。
cues.en: And we think a lot about many of the other things we’ve got to get right for AGI, but thinking about how to build a resilient org and how to build a structure that will stand up to a lot of pressure in the world, which I expect more and more as we get closer, I think that’s super important.

cues.zh: 你觉得董事会的审议过程有多深入、多严谨？
cues.en: Do you have a sense of how deep and rigorous the deliberation process by the board was?

cues.zh: 你能谈谈这种情况下涉及的人性动态吗？
cues.en: Can you shine some light on just human dynamics involved in situations like this?

cues.zh: 是不是就几次对话，然后突然就升级了，为什么不开除Sam之类的？
cues.en: Was it just a few conversations and all of a sudden it escalates and why don’t we fire Sam kind of thing?

cues.zh: 我认为董事会成员总体上是善意的，我相信在压力大的情况下，当人们感到时间紧迫或其他压力时，人们会理解并做出次优决策。
cues.en: I think the board members are well-meaning people on the whole, and I believe that in stressful situations where people feel time pressure or whatever, people understand and make suboptimal decisions.

cues.zh: 我认为OpenAI面临的挑战之一将是，我们必须有一个善于在压力下运作的董事会和团队。
cues.en: And I think one of the challenges for OpenAI will be we’re going to have to have a board and a team that are good at operating under pressure.

cues.zh: 你觉得董事会权力过大吗？
cues.en: Do you think the board had too much power?

cues.zh: 我认为董事会本应拥有很大权力，但我们看到的一件事是，在大多数公司结构中，董事会通常对股东负责。
cues.en: I think boards are supposed to have a lot of power, but one of the things that we did see is in most corporate structures, boards are usually answerable to shareholders.

cues.zh: 有时候人们会有超级投票权股份之类的安排。
cues.en: Sometimes people have super voting shares or whatever.

cues.zh: 在这种情况下，我觉得我们的结构里有一点或许当初应该多考虑一些，那就是非营利组织的董事会，除非你另设其他规则，否则拥有相当大的权力。
cues.en: In this case, and I think one of the things with our structure that we maybe should have thought about more than we did is that the board of a nonprofit has, unless you put other rules in place, quite a lot of power.

cues.zh: 他们实际上只对自己负责。
cues.en: They don’t really answer to anyone but themselves.

cues.zh: 这种安排有它的好处，但我们真正希望的是，OpenAI的董事会能对整个世界负责，尽可能做到这一点。
cues.en: And there’s ways in which that’s good, but what we’d really like is for the board of OpenAI to answer to the world as a whole, as much as that’s a practical thing.

cues.zh: 所以现在宣布了一个新董事会。
cues.en: So there’s a new board announced.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我猜一开始是一个新的规模较小的董事会，现在又有了一个新的最终董事会？
cues.en: There’s I guess a new smaller board at first, and now there’s a new final board?

cues.zh: 还不是最终董事会。
cues.en: Not a final board yet.

cues.zh: 我们已经增加了一些成员。
cues.en: We’ve added some.

cues.zh: 还会继续增加。
cues.en: We’ll add more.

cues.zh: 增加了一些。
cues.en: Added some.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 新董事会里固定下来、而之前那个可能存在问题的地方是什么？
cues.en: What is fixed in the new one that was perhaps broken in the previous one?

cues.zh: 大约一年间，旧董事会规模逐渐缩小。
cues.en: The old board got smaller over the course of about a year.

cues.zh: 起初有九人，后来减到六人，接着对于该增补谁又无法达成一致。
cues.en: It was nine and then it went down to six, and then we couldn’t agree on who to add.

cues.zh: 而且我认为董事会里经验丰富的成员不多，OpenAI新加入的很多董事在董事会经验上更为丰富。
cues.en: And the board also I think didn’t have a lot of experienced board members, and a lot of the new board members at OpenAI have just have more experience as board members.

cues.zh: 我觉得那会有帮助。
cues.en: I think that’ll help.

cues.zh: 有人批评说，一些加入董事会的人选有问题。
cues.en: It’s been criticized, some of the people that are added to the board.

cues.zh: 比如，我听到很多人批评拉里·萨默斯的加入。
cues.en: I heard a lot of people criticizing the addition of Larry Summers, for example.

cues.zh: 挑选董事会的流程是怎样的？
cues.en: What’s the process of selecting the board?

cues.zh: 其中涉及哪些环节？
cues.en: What’s involved in that?

cues.zh: 布雷特和拉里是在那个紧张周末的紧要关头决定的，那个周末真是跌宕起伏。
cues.en: So Brett and Larry were decided in the heat of the moment over this very tense weekend, and that weekend was a real rollercoaster.

cues.zh: 经历了许多起起落落。
cues.en: It was a lot of ups and downs.

cues.zh: 我们当时正努力就新董事会成员达成一致，既要让这里的高管团队觉得合理，也要让老董事会成员觉得合理。
cues.en: And we were trying to agree on new board members that both the executive team here and the old board members felt would be reasonable.

cues.zh: Larry其实是老董事会成员那边推荐的人选之一。
cues.en: Larry was actually one of their suggestions, the old board members.

cues.zh: Brett，我想在那周末之前我就已经提过他了，但他很忙，不想做，后来我们在[听不清 00:09:22]方面确实需要帮助。
cues.en: Brett, I think I had even previous to that weekend suggested, but he was busy and didn’t want to do it, and then we really needed help in [inaudible 00:09:22].

cues.zh: 我们也谈了很多其他人，但我觉得如果我要回来，就需要新的董事会成员。
cues.en: We talked about a lot of other people too, but I felt like if I was going to come back, I needed new board members.

cues.zh: 我不认为我能以同样的配置再和老董事会合作，尽管后来我们决定，而且我很感激Adam愿意留下，但我们考虑了各种配置，决定要组成一个三人的董事会，并且必须在很短的时间内找到两名新董事会成员。
cues.en: I didn’t think I could work with the old board again in the same configuration, although we then decided, and I’m grateful that Adam would stay, but we considered various configurations, decided we wanted to get to a board of three and had to find two new board members over the course of a short period of time.

cues.zh: 所以那些决定是诚实地做出的，没有……那是在战场上做的。
cues.en: So those were decided honestly without… You do that on the battlefield.

cues.zh: 那时你没时间设计严谨的流程。
cues.en: You don’t have time to design a rigorous process then.

cues.zh: 对于后来的新董事会成员，以及我们未来将增加的新成员，我们有一些认为董事会有必要具备的标准，希望董事会拥有不同的专业知识。
cues.en: For new board members since, and new board members we’ll add going forward, we have some criteria that we think are important for the board to have, different expertise that we want the board to have.

cues.zh: 不像招聘高管，你需要他们做好一个角色，董事会需要做好治理和深思熟虑的整个角色，所以，Brett说的一点我很喜欢，就是我们希望以团队形式招聘董事会成员，而不是一次一个地招个人。
cues.en: Unlike hiring an executive where you need them to do one role well, the board needs to do a whole role of governance and thoughtfulness well, and so, one thing that Brett says which I really like is that we want to hire board members in slates, not as individuals one at a time.

cues.zh: 考虑一群能带来非营利组织专业知识、经营公司专业知识、良好法律和治理专业知识的人，这就是我们努力优化的方向。
cues.en: And thinking about a group of people that will bring nonprofit expertise, expertise at running companies, good legal and governance expertise, that’s what we’ve tried to optimize for.

cues.zh: 那么，对每位董事会成员来说，技术素养都很重要吗？
cues.en: So is technical savvy important for the individual board members?

cues.zh: 并非每位董事会成员都需要，但肯定有些成员必须具备。
cues.en: Not for every board member, but for certainly some you need that.

cues.zh: 这是董事会职责的一部分。
cues.en: That’s part of what the board needs to do.

cues.zh: 关于 OpenAI，人们可能不了解的有趣之处——我当然也不了解——是运营业务的所有细节。
cues.en: The interesting thing that people probably don’t understand about OpenAI, I certainly don’t, is all the details of running the business.

cues.zh: 考虑到那场风波，他们想到董事会时，就会想到你。
cues.en: When they think about the board, given the drama, they think about you.

cues.zh: 他们会想，如果你实现了 AGI，或者做出了某些极具影响力的产品并完成构建和部署，那时与董事会的对话会是什么样？
cues.en: They think about if you reach AGI or you reach some of these incredibly impactful products and you build them and deploy them, what’s the conversation with the board like?

cues.zh: 他们会想，好吧，在这种情况下，应该组建什么样的合适团队来商议？
cues.en: And they think, all right, what’s the right squad to have in that kind of situation to deliberate?

cues.zh: 你看，我认为那里确实需要一些技术专家。
cues.en: Look, I think you definitely need some technical experts there.

cues.zh: 然后你还需要一些人，他们会想：“我们怎样才能以最能帮助世人的方式部署这项技术？”以及一些视角非常不同的人。
cues.en: And then you need some people who are like, “How can we deploy this in a way that will help people in the world the most?” And people who have a very different perspective.

cues.zh: 我觉得你或我可能犯的一个错误，就是以为只有技术层面的理解才重要，这当然是你希望那个董事会进行的对话的一部分，但还有很多关于这将如何影响社会和人们生活的内容，你确实也希望在那里得到体现。
cues.en: I think a mistake that you or I might make is to think that only the technical understanding matters, and that’s definitely part of the conversation you want that board to have, but there’s a lot more about how that’s going to just impact society and people’s lives that you really want represented in there too.

cues.zh: 你是看人们的过往履历，还是只是进行交谈？
cues.en: Are you looking at the track record of people or you’re just having conversations?

cues.zh: 过往履历很重要。
cues.en: Track record is a big deal.

cues.zh: 你当然会进行很多交谈，但有些职位我会完全忽略过往履历，只看斜率，忽略Y轴截距。
cues.en: You of course have a lot of conversations, but there are some roles where I totally ignore track record and just look at slope, ignore the Y-intercept.

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: 谢谢您为观众做了数学化的讲解。
cues.en: Thank you for making it mathematical for the audience.

cues.zh: 作为董事会成员，我更关心的是Y轴截距。
cues.en: For a board member, I do care much more about the Y-intercept.

cues.zh: 我觉得关于过往业绩这一点有很深的东西可讲，而经验是某种很难被替代的东西。
cues.en: I think there is something deep to say about track record there, and experience is something’s very hard to replace.

cues.zh: 您会尝试用多项式函数还是指数函数来拟合过往业绩？
cues.en: Do you try to fit a polynomial function or exponential one to the track record?

cues.zh: 这个类比推不了那么远。
cues.en: That analogy doesn’t carry that far.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 您提到了那个周末的一些低谷时刻。
cues.en: You mentioned some of the low points that weekend.

cues.zh: 从心理层面来说，您的一些低谷是什么？
cues.en: What were some of the low points psychologically for you?

cues.zh: 您有没有考虑过去亚马逊丛林，就喝点死藤水然后永远消失？
cues.en: Did you consider going to the Amazon jungle and just taking ayahuasca and disappearing forever?

cues.zh: 那是一段非常糟糕的时期。
cues.en: It was a very bad period of time.

cues.zh: 也有过非常棒的高光时刻。
cues.en: There were great high points too.

cues.zh: 我的手机不停地被消息轰炸，都是每天共事的人发来的暖心话，还有十年没联系过的人。
cues.en: My phone was just nonstop blowing up with nice messages from people I worked with every day, people I hadn’t talked to in a decade.

cues.zh: 我没能好好体会那份美好，因为当时正忙于这场激烈的交锋，但那确实很棒。
cues.en: I didn’t get to appreciate that as much as I should have because I was just in the middle of this firefight, but that was really nice.

cues.zh: 但总的来说，那是个非常痛苦的周末。
cues.en: But on the whole, it was a very painful weekend.

cues.zh: 那就像一场出乎意料地公开进行的战斗，对我来说极其消耗精力，远超我的预期。
cues.en: It was like a battle fought in public to a surprising degree, and that was extremely exhausting to me, much more than I expected.

cues.zh: 我觉得争斗通常都很累人，但这一次真的特别累。
cues.en: I think fights are generally exhausting, but this one really was.

cues.zh: 董事会是在周五下午做出这个决定的。
cues.en: The board did this Friday afternoon.

cues.zh: 我确实没能得到多少答案，但我当时也想，好吧，董事会有权这么做，所以我会花点时间想想自己想做什么，但我会试着从中找到好的一面。
cues.en: I really couldn’t get much in the way of answers, but I also was just like, well, the board gets to do this, so I’m going to think for a little bit about what I want to do, but I’ll try to find the blessing in disguise here.

cues.zh: 我当时想，好吧，我目前在 OpenAI 的工作，或者说曾经的工作，是在这个阶段经营一家规模不小的公司。
cues.en: And I was like, well, my current job at OpenAI is, or it was, to run a decently sized company at this point.

cues.zh: 我最喜欢的始终是能和研究人员一起工作。
cues.en: And the thing I’d always liked the most was just getting to work with the researchers.

cues.zh: 我当时想，是啊，我可以直接去做一个非常聚焦的AGI研究项目。
cues.en: And I was like, yeah, I can just go do a very focused AGI research effort.

cues.zh: 我为此很兴奋。
cues.en: And I got excited about that.

cues.zh: 当时我甚至完全没想到，这一切可能会被全部推翻。
cues.en: Didn’t even occur to me at the time possibly that this was all going to get undone.

cues.zh: 那是周五下午。
cues.en: This was Friday afternoon.

cues.zh: 所以你已经接受了这件事的终结——
cues.en: So you’ve accepted the death of this-

cues.zh: 非常快。
cues.en: Very quickly.

cues.zh: 非常快。
cues.en: Very quickly.

cues.zh: 我经历了一小段困惑和愤怒的时期，但非常快，非常快。
cues.en: I went through a little period of confusion and rage, but very quickly, quickly.

cues.zh: 到了周五晚上，我已经在和人们讨论接下来要做什么了，我对此很兴奋。
cues.en: And by Friday night, I was talking to people about what was going to be next, and I was excited about that.

cues.zh: 我想是周五晚上，我第一次听到这里的高管团队说：“嘿，我们要抗争这件事。”然后我去睡觉时仍然觉得，好吧，很兴奋。
cues.en: I think it was Friday evening for the first time that I heard from the exec team here, which is like, “Hey, we’re going to fight this.” and then I went to bed just still being like, okay, excited.

cues.zh: 继续。
cues.en: Onward.

cues.zh: 你睡着了吗？
cues.en: Were you able to sleep?

cues.zh: 没怎么睡。
cues.en: Not a lot.

cues.zh: 奇怪的是，有四天半时间我几乎没怎么睡、没怎么吃，精力却出奇地旺盛。
cues.en: One of the weird things was there was this period of four and a half days where I didn’t sleep much, didn’t eat much, and still had a surprising amount of energy.

cues.zh: 战时你对肾上腺素会有种奇怪的体会。
cues.en: You learn a weird thing about adrenaline in wartime.

cues.zh: 所以你接受了这个“孩子”——OpenAI——的死亡。
cues.en: So you accepted the death of this baby, OpenAI.

cues.zh: 而我当时对新事物充满期待。
cues.en: And I was excited for the new thing.

cues.zh: 我心想：“好吧，这事挺疯狂的，但无所谓了。”
cues.en: I was just like, “Okay, this was crazy, but whatever.”

cues.zh: 这是一种很好的应对机制。
cues.en: It’s a very good coping mechanism.

cues.zh: 然后周六早上，两位董事会成员打来电话说：“嘿，我们不是想搞乱局面。
cues.en: And then Saturday morning, two of the board members called and said, “Hey, we didn’t mean to destabilize things.

cues.zh: 我们不想在这里存储太多价值。
cues.en: We don’t want to store a lot of value here.

cues.zh: 能谈谈你回来的事吗？”我立刻就不想回去，但多想了一会儿后，我觉得，我真的很在乎这里的人、合作伙伴和股东。
cues.en: Can we talk about you coming back?” And I immediately didn’t want to do that, but I thought a little more and I was like, well, I really care about the people here, the partners, shareholders.

cues.zh: 我爱这家公司。
cues.en: I love this company.

cues.zh: 于是我想了想，我说：“好吧，但我需要这些东西。”而最痛苦的时刻是那个周末，我一直在思考，也不断被告知——不只是我，整个团队都在想，我们努力让 OpenAI 保持稳定，而全世界都在试图把它拆散，有人试图挖人什么的。
cues.en: And so I thought about it and I was like, “Well, okay, but here’s the stuff I would need.” And then the most painful time of all was over the course of that weekend, I kept thinking and being told, and not just me, the whole team here kept thinking, well, we were trying to keep OpenAI stabilized while the whole world was trying to break it apart, people trying to recruit whatever.

cues.zh: 我们不断被告知，好了，我们快完成了。
cues.en: We kept being told, all right, we’re almost done.

cues.zh: 我们快完成了。
cues.en: We’re almost done.

cues.zh: 我们只是需要再多一点时间。
cues.en: We just need a little bit more time.

cues.zh: 那是一种非常令人困惑的状态。
cues.en: And it was this very confusing state.

cues.zh: 然后到了周日晚上，每隔几个小时我都以为我们要完成了，我们会找到办法让我回来，让一切恢复原样。
cues.en: And then Sunday evening when, again, every few hours I expected that we were going to be done and we’re going to figure out a way for me to return and things to go back to how they were.

cues.zh: 董事会随后任命了一位新的临时CEO，我当时就觉得，这感觉真的很糟糕。
cues.en: The board then appointed a new interim CEO, and then I was like, that feels really bad.

cues.zh: 那是整件事的最低谷。
cues.en: That was the low point of the whole thing.

cues.zh: 我跟你说件事。
cues.en: I’ll tell you something.

cues.zh: 那感觉很痛苦，但整个周末我感受到了很多爱。
cues.en: It felt very painful, but I felt a lot of love that whole weekend.

cues.zh: 除了周日晚上那一刻，我不会把自己的情绪形容为愤怒或仇恨，但我感受到了人们之间大量的爱。
cues.en: Other than that one moment Sunday night, I would not characterize my emotions as anger or hate, but I felt a lot of love from people, towards people.

cues.zh: 那很痛苦，但那个周末的主导情绪是爱，不是恨。
cues.en: It was painful, but the dominant emotion of the weekend was love, not hate.

cues.zh: 你对Mira Murati评价很高，说她特别在关键时刻、正如你在推文里说的，在那些安静的时刻帮了大忙。
cues.en: You’ve spoken highly of Mira Murati, that she helped especially, as you put in the tweet, in the quiet moments when it counts.

cues.zh: 也许我们可以稍微岔开一下话题。
cues.en: Perhaps we could take a bit of a tangent.

cues.zh: 你欣赏Mira的什么？
cues.en: What do you admire about Mira?

cues.zh: 嗯，那个周末一片混乱，她做得非常出色，但人们往往在危机时刻才看到领导者，无论好坏。
cues.en: Well, she did a great job during that weekend in a lot of chaos, but people often see leaders in the crisis moments, good or bad.

cues.zh: 但我真正看重领导者的，是人们在平淡无奇的周二早上9点46分、在日常的琐碎事务中如何行事。
cues.en: But a thing I really value in leaders is how people act on a boring Tuesday at 9:46 in the morning and in just the normal drudgery of the day-to-day.

cues.zh: 一个人在会议上的表现，以及他们所做决策的质量。
cues.en: How someone shows up in a meeting, the quality of the decisions they make.

cues.zh: 这就是我说的那些安静时刻。
cues.en: That was what I meant about the quiet moments.

cues.zh: 意思是大部分工作都是一天一天、一场会一场会地完成的。
cues.en: Meaning most of the work is done on a day-by-day, in meeting-by-meeting.

cues.zh: 就是到场，做出好的决策。
cues.en: Just be present and make great decisions.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 你看，你过去20分钟一直想聊的，我理解，是这个戏剧性的周末，但那并不是OpenAI的真正意义所在。
cues.en: Look, what you have wanted to spend the last 20 minutes about, and I understand, is this one very dramatic weekend, but that’s not really what OpenAI is about.

cues.zh: OpenAI真正的意义在于另外那七年。
cues.en: OpenAI is really about the other seven years.

cues.zh: 嗯，是的。
cues.en: Well, yeah.

cues.zh: 人类文明并不只是纳粹德国入侵苏联，但那仍然是人们关注的焦点。
cues.en: Human civilization is not about the invasion of the Soviet Union by Nazi Germany, but still that’s something people focus on.

cues.zh: 非常容易理解。
cues.en: Very understandable.

cues.zh: 它让我们洞察人性，洞察人性的极端，也许人类文明某些成就中的一些损害就发生在那些时刻，所以它很有启发性。
cues.en: It gives us an insight into human nature, the extremes of human nature, and perhaps some of the damage in some of the triumphs of human civilization can happen in those moments, so it’s illustrative.

cues.zh: 让我问问你关于Ilya的事。
cues.en: Let me ask you about Ilya.

cues.zh: 他是不是被扣在一个秘密核设施里当人质？
cues.en: Is he being held hostage in a secret nuclear facility?

cues.zh: 没有。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 那普通的秘密设施呢？
cues.en: What about a regular secret facility?

cues.zh: 没有。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 那非秘密的核设施呢？
cues.en: What about a nuclear non-secret facility?

cues.zh: 都不是。
cues.en: Neither.

cues.zh: 也不是那个。
cues.en: Not that either.

cues.zh: 这迟早会变成一个梗。
cues.en: This is becoming a meme at some point.

cues.zh: 你认识Ilya很久了。
cues.en: You’ve known Ilya for a long time.

cues.zh: 他显然卷入了董事会那场风波之类的事情。
cues.en: He was obviously part of this drama with the board and all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 你现在和他是什么关系？
cues.en: What’s your relationship with him now?

cues.zh: 我爱Ilya。
cues.en: I love Ilya.

cues.zh: 我非常尊重Ilya。
cues.en: I have tremendous respect for Ilya.

cues.zh: 关于他目前的计划，我现在没什么能说的。
cues.en: I don’t have anything I can say about his plans right now.

cues.zh: 这是他该回答的问题，但我真的希望我们至少在我余下的职业生涯里都能一起合作。
cues.en: That’s a question for him, but I really hope we work together for certainly the rest of my career.

cues.zh: 他比我年轻一点。
cues.en: He’s a little bit younger than me.

cues.zh: 也许他工作的时间更长一点。
cues.en: Maybe he works a little bit longer.

cues.zh: 有个梗说他看到了什么东西，比如他可能看到了AGI，这让他内心非常担忧。
cues.en: There’s a meme that he saw something, like he maybe saw AGI and that gave him a lot of worry internally.

cues.zh: Ilya看到了什么？
cues.en: What did Ilya see?

cues.zh: Ilya并没有看到AGI。
cues.en: Ilya has not seen AGI.

cues.zh: 我们谁都没看到AGI。
cues.en: None of us have seen AGI.

cues.zh: 我们还没有造出AGI。
cues.en: We’ve not built AGI.

cues.zh: 我确实认为，我特别喜欢Ilya的一点是，他非常认真地对待AGI和安全方面的担忧，广义上讲，包括这将对社会产生的影响。
cues.en: I do think one of the many things that I really love about Ilya is he takes AGI and the safety concerns, broadly speaking, including things like the impact this is going to have on society, very seriously.

cues.zh: 随着我们不断取得重大进展，过去几年里，我和Ilya花最多时间讨论的就是这意味着什么，我们需要做什么来确保我们做对，确保我们完成使命。
cues.en: And as we continue to make significant progress, Ilya is one of the people that I’ve spent the most time over the last couple of years talking about what this is going to mean, what we need to do to ensure we get it right, to ensure that we succeed at the mission.

cues.zh: 所以 Ilya 并没有看到 AGI，但就他投入了多少思考、多么担心要把这件事做对而言，Ilya 是人类的光荣。
cues.en: So Ilya did not see AGI, but Ilya is a credit to humanity in terms of how much he thinks and worries about making sure we get this right.

cues.zh: 我过去和他有过很多次交流。
cues.en: I’ve had a bunch of conversation with him in the past.

cues.zh: 我觉得他谈技术的时候，总是做这种长期思考。
cues.en: I think when he talks about technology, he’s always doing this long-term thinking type of thing.

cues.zh: 所以他想的不是一年后会怎样。
cues.en: So he is not thinking about what this is going to be in a year.

cues.zh: 他想的是十年后，纯粹从第一性原理出发去想，“好，如果这东西规模化，这里的基本原理是什么？
cues.en: He’s thinking about in 10 years, just thinking from first principles like, “Okay, if this scales, what are the fundamentals here?

cues.zh: 这会走向哪里？”这就成了他们思考其他所有安全关切之类问题的基础，也让他成为一个聊起来非常有意思的人。
cues.en: Where’s this going?” And so that’s a foundation for them thinking about all the other safety concerns and all that kind of stuff, which makes him a really fascinating human to talk with.

cues.zh: 你知道他为什么一直很安静吗？
cues.en: Do you have any idea why he’s been quiet?

cues.zh: 他是不是只是在自我反省？
cues.en: Is it he’s just doing some soul-searching?

cues.zh: 再说一次，我不想代表Ilya发言。
cues.en: Again, I don’t want to speak for Ilya.

cues.zh: 我觉得这个问题你应该去问他。
cues.en: I think that you should ask him that.

cues.zh: 他绝对是个心思缜密的人。
cues.en: He’s definitely a thoughtful guy.

cues.zh: 我觉得Ilya一直以一种非常好的方式在自我探索。
cues.en: I think Ilya is always on a soul search in a really good way.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 而且，他很懂得沉默的力量。
cues.en: Also, he appreciates the power of silence.

cues.zh: 还有，我听说他也可以很搞怪，但我从没见过他那一面。
cues.en: Also, I’m told he can be a silly guy, which I’ve never seen that side of him.

cues.zh: 那种时候真的很可爱。
cues.en: It’s very sweet when that happens.

cues.zh: 我从没见过搞怪的Ilya，但我也很期待看到。
cues.en: I’ve never witnessed a silly Ilya, but I look forward to that as well.

cues.zh: 我最近和他一起参加了个晚宴，他在跟一只小狗玩，心情特别搞怪，非常讨人喜欢。
cues.en: I was at a dinner party with him recently and he was playing with a puppy and he was in a very silly mood, very endearing.

cues.zh: 我当时在想，天哪，这可不是世界最常看到的Ilya那一面。
cues.en: And I was thinking, oh man, this is not the side of Ilya that the world sees the most.

cues.zh: 那么，总结一下这整件事，你对董事会结构满意吗——
cues.en: So just to wrap up this whole saga, are you feeling good about the board structure-

cues.zh: 满意。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: ……关于这一切以及它的走向？
cues.en: … about all of this and where it’s moving?

cues.zh: 我对新的董事会感觉很好。
cues.en: I feel great about the new board.

cues.zh: 就 OpenAI 的结构而言，董事会的任务之一就是审视这一点，看看我们能在哪些方面让它更稳健。
cues.en: In terms of the structure of OpenAI, one of the board’s tasks is to look at that and see where we can make it more robust.

cues.zh: 我们本想先让新董事会成员到位，但整个过程中我们显然在结构上学到了教训。
cues.en: We wanted to get new board members in place first, but we clearly learned a lesson about structure throughout this process.

cues.zh: 我觉得我没有什么特别深刻的见解要说。
cues.en: I don’t have, I think, super deep things to say.

cues.zh: 那是一段疯狂、非常痛苦的经历。
cues.en: It was a crazy, very painful experience.

cues.zh: 我觉得那是各种怪异因素叠加的完美风暴。
cues.en: I think it was a perfect storm of weirdness.

cues.zh: 对我来说，这像是一次预演，预示了随着利害关系越来越高、我们对稳健治理结构、流程和人员的需求会变成什么样。
cues.en: It was a preview for me of what’s going to happen as the stakes get higher and higher and the need that we have robust governance structures and processes and people.

cues.zh: 我很高兴它发生在那个时候，但经历它确实是痛苦得令人震惊。
cues.en: I’m happy it happened when it did, but it was a shockingly painful thing to go through.

cues.zh: 这件事让你更不敢轻易信任别人了吗？
cues.en: Did it make you be more hesitant in trusting people?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 只是个人层面上的？
cues.en: Just on a personal level?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 我觉得我原本是个极其容易信任别人的人。
cues.en: I think I’m like an extremely trusting person.

cues.zh: 我一直的人生哲学就是不去操心那些疑神疑鬼的事。
cues.en: I’ve always had a life philosophy of don’t worry about all of the paranoia.

cues.zh: 不去操心那些极端情况。
cues.en: Don’t worry about the edge cases.

cues.zh: 你稍微吃点亏，换来的是可以放下戒备地生活。
cues.en: You get a little bit screwed in exchange for getting to live with your guard down.

cues.zh: 而这件事让我太震惊了。
cues.en: And this was so shocking to me.

cues.zh: 我完全措手不及，它确实改变了我，我真的很不喜欢这样，它确实改变了我对默认信任别人和防范坏情况的看法。
cues.en: I was so caught off guard that it has definitely changed, and I really don’t like this, it’s definitely changed how I think about just default trust of people and planning for the bad scenarios.

cues.zh: 这方面你得小心。
cues.en: You got to be careful with that.

cues.zh: 你担心自己会变得有点太愤世嫉俗吗？
cues.en: Are you worried about becoming a little too cynical?

cues.zh: 我不担心自己变得太愤世嫉俗。
cues.en: I’m not worried about becoming too cynical.

cues.zh: 我觉得我和愤世嫉俗的人恰恰相反，但我担心自己会变得不再那么默认信任别人。
cues.en: I think I’m the extreme opposite of a cynical person, but I’m worried about just becoming less of a default trusting person.

cues.zh: 其实我不确定，对于开发AGI的人来说，哪种模式最适合运作——信任还是不信任。
cues.en: I’m actually not sure which mode is best to operate in for a person who’s developing AGI, trusting or un-trusting.

cues.zh: 你正踏上一段有趣的旅程。
cues.en: It’s an interesting journey you’re on.

cues.zh: 但就结构而言，我更关注人的层面。
cues.en: But in terms of structure, see, I’m more interested on the human level.

cues.zh: 你如何让自己身边围绕着那些在打造酷东西、同时又做出明智决策的人？
cues.en: How do you surround yourself with humans that are building cool shit, but also are making wise decisions?

cues.zh: 因为你赚的钱越多，这东西拥有的权力越大，人就会变得越古怪。
cues.en: Because the more money you start making, the more power the thing has, the weirder people get.

cues.zh: 我觉得你可以对董事会成员、对我本应拥有的信任程度、或者对我本该怎么做事，发表各种各样的评论。
cues.en: I think you could make all kinds of comments about the board members and the level of trust I should have had there, or how I should have done things differently.

cues.zh: 但就这里的团队而言，我认为这方面你得给我打个很高的分。
cues.en: But in terms of the team here, I think you’d have to give me a very good grade on that one.

cues.zh: 我对我每天共事的人怀有巨大的感激、信任和尊重，我认为身边围绕着这样的人真的非常重要。
cues.en: And I have just enormous gratitude and trust and respect for the people that I work with every day, and I think being surrounded with people like that is really important.

cues.zh: 我们的共同朋友Elon起诉了OpenAI。
cues.en: Our mutual friend Elon sued OpenAI.

cues.zh: 在你看来，他批评的核心是什么？
cues.en: What to you is the essence of what he’s criticizing?

cues.zh: 他的话有几分道理？
cues.en: To what degree does he have a point?

cues.zh: 又有几分是错的？
cues.en: To what degree is he wrong?

cues.zh: 我不知道这到底是为了什么。
cues.en: I don’t know what it’s really about.

cues.zh: 我们起初只想着做一个研究实验室，对这项技术会如何发展毫无头绪。
cues.en: We started off just thinking we were going to be a research lab and having no idea about how this technology was going to go.

cues.zh: 因为那不过是七八年前的事，很难回想当时的确切情形，但那时语言模型还没成为什么大事。
cues.en: Because it was only seven or eight years ago, it’s hard to go back and really remember what it was like then, but this is before language models were a big deal.

cues.zh: 那时我们还没想过API，也没想过出售聊天机器人的访问权限。
cues.en: This was before we had any idea about an API or selling access to a chatbot.

cues.zh: 那时我们压根没想过要做成产品。
cues.en: It was before we had any idea we were going to productize at all.

cues.zh: 所以我们想，“我们就试着做研究吧，并不真清楚要拿它干什么。”我想，面对许多全新的东西，你都是在黑暗中摸索，做出一些假设，而其中大部分后来都被证明是错的。
cues.en: So we’re like, “We’re just going to try to do research and we don’t really know what we’re going to do with that.” I think with many fundamentally new things, you start fumbling through the dark and you make some assumptions, most of which turned out to be wrong.

cues.zh: 然后事情就很清楚了，我们需要做不同的事情，还需要大量得多的资金。
cues.en: And then it became clear that we were going to need to do different things and also have huge amounts more capital.

cues.zh: 于是我们说：“好吧，这个结构不太适合那个目标。
cues.en: So we said, “Okay, well, the structure doesn’t quite work for that.

cues.zh: 我们怎么给这个结构打补丁？”然后你打一个补丁，再打一个补丁，最后得到的东西至少可以说看起来让人侧目。
cues.en: How do we patch the structure?” And then you patch it again and patch it again and you end up with something that does look eyebrow-raising, to say the least.

cues.zh: 但我们是一步步走到这里的，我认为沿途每一步都做了合理的决定。
cues.en: But we got here gradually with, I think, reasonable decisions at each point along the way.

cues.zh: 这并不意味着如果现在能带着先知回去，我不会完全换个做法，但当时你并没有先知。
cues.en: And it doesn’t mean I wouldn’t do it totally differently if we could go back now with an Oracle, but you don’t get the Oracle at the time.

cues.zh: 不过无论如何，至于Elon在这里的真实动机是什么，我不知道。
cues.en: But anyway, in terms of what Elon’s real motivations here are, I don’t know.

cues.zh: 你还记得的话，OpenAI在那篇博客文章里给出的回应是什么？
cues.en: To the degree you remember, what was the response that OpenAI gave in the blog post?

cues.zh: 你能总结一下吗？
cues.en: Can you summarize it?

cues.zh: 哦，我们刚说了，Elon 说过这一系列的话。
cues.en: Oh, we just said Elon said this set of things.

cues.zh: 这是我们的描述，或者说不是我们的描述。
cues.en: Here’s our characterization, or here’s not our characterization.

cues.zh: 这是对事情经过的描述。
cues.en: Here’s the characterization of how this went down.

cues.zh: 我们尽量不把它弄得情绪化，只是说：“这是事情的经过。”
cues.en: We tried to not make it emotional and just say, “Here’s the history.”

cues.zh: 我确实认为，Elon 对你刚才提到的其中一点有一定程度的歪曲，那就是当时你们的不确定性有多大。
cues.en: I do think there’s a degree of mischaracterization from Elon here about one of the points you just made, which is the degree of uncertainty you had at the time.

cues.zh: 你们是一小群研究者，疯狂地谈论 AGI，而当时所有人都在嘲笑这个想法。
cues.en: You guys are a small group of researchers crazily talking about AGI when everybody’s laughing at that thought.

cues.zh: 不久前，Elon 还在疯狂地谈论发射火箭，当时人们也在嘲笑这个想法，所以我觉得他对此应该更有同理心。
cues.en: It wasn’t that long ago Elon was crazily talking about launching rockets when people were laughing at that thought, so I think he’d have more empathy for this.

cues.zh: 我确实认为这里面有个人因素，就是出现了一次分裂，OpenAI 和这里很多优秀的人选择与 Elon 分道扬镳，所以这里有个人层面的——
cues.en: I do think that there’s personal stuff here, that there was a split that OpenAI and a lot of amazing people here chose to part ways with Elon, so there’s a personal-

cues.zh: 是 Elon 选择分道扬镳的。
cues.en: Elon chose to part ways.

cues.zh: 你能具体描述一下吗？
cues.en: Can you describe that exactly?

cues.zh: 选择分道扬镳？
cues.en: The choosing to part ways?

cues.zh: 他认为OpenAI会失败。
cues.en: He thought OpenAI was going to fail.

cues.zh: 他想要完全控制权来扭转局面。
cues.en: He wanted total control to turn it around.

cues.zh: 我们想继续沿着如今成为OpenAI的方向前进。
cues.en: We wanted to keep going in the direction that now has become OpenAI.

cues.zh: 他还希望Tesla能够开展AGI方面的工作。
cues.en: He also wanted Tesla to be able to build an AGI effort.

cues.zh: 在不同时期，他想把OpenAI变成一家他能控制的营利性公司，或者让它与Tesla合并。
cues.en: At various times, he wanted to make OpenAI into a for-profit company that he could have control of or have it merge with Tesla.

cues.zh: 我们不想那样做，于是他决定离开，这没问题。
cues.en: We didn’t want to do that, and he decided to leave, which that’s fine.

cues.zh: 所以你是说，这也是博客文章提到的其中一点，就是他希望OpenAI基本上被Tesla收购，方式类似于，或者可能类似，或者可能比与Microsoft的合作更戏剧化。
cues.en: So you’re saying, and that’s one of the things that the blog post says, is that he wanted OpenAI to be basically acquired by Tesla in the same way that, or maybe something similar or maybe something more dramatic than the partnership with Microsoft.

cues.zh: 我记得当时的提议就是，对，让特斯拉收购它，由特斯拉完全控制。
cues.en: My memory is the proposal was just like, yeah, get acquired by Tesla and have Tesla have full control over it.

cues.zh: 我很确定就是这样。
cues.en: I’m pretty sure that’s what it was.

cues.zh: 那么当时对埃隆来说，OpenAI 里“Open”这个词是什么意思？
cues.en: So what does the word open in OpenAI mean to Elon at the time?

cues.zh: 伊利亚在邮件往来之类的内容里谈过这个。
cues.en: Ilya has talked about this in the email exchanges and all this kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 当时对你来说是什么意思？
cues.en: What does it mean to you at the time?

cues.zh: 现在对你来说又是什么意思？
cues.en: What does it mean to you now?

cues.zh: 说到带着 Oracle 回去，我会选个不同的名字。
cues.en: Speaking of going back with an Oracle, I’d pick a different name.

cues.zh: 我认为 OpenAI 在做的事情中，最重要的一件就是把强大的技术免费交到人们手中，作为公共福祉。
cues.en: One of the things that I think OpenAI is doing that is the most important of everything that we’re doing is putting powerful technology in the hands of people for free, as a public good.

cues.zh: 我们不在我们的——
cues.en: We don’t run ads on our-

cues.zh: ……作为公共福祉。
cues.en: … as a public good.

cues.zh: 我们的免费版不投放广告。
cues.en: We don’t run ads on our free version.

cues.zh: 我们也不通过其他方式变现。
cues.en: We don’t monetize it in other ways.

cues.zh: 我们只说这是使命的一部分。
cues.en: We just say it’s part of our mission.

cues.zh: 我们想把越来越强大的工具免费交到人们手中，让他们去使用。
cues.en: We want to put increasingly powerful tools in the hands of people for free and get them to use them.

cues.zh: 我认为这种开放对我们的使命非常重要。
cues.en: I think that kind of open is really important to our mission.

cues.zh: 我觉得，如果你给人们好工具，教他们怎么用，甚至不教，他们自己也能摸索出来，然后让他们用这些工具为彼此构建不可思议的未来，这意义重大。
cues.en: I think if you give people great tools and teach them to use them or don’t even teach them, they’ll figure it out, and let them go build an incredible future for each other with that, that’s a big deal.

cues.zh: 所以，如果我们能持续把免费或低成本、甚至免费且低成本的强大 AI 工具推向世界，我认为这对我们如何完成使命意义重大。
cues.en: So if we can keep putting free or low cost or free and low cost powerful AI tools out in the world, I think that’s a huge deal for how we fulfill the mission.

cues.zh: 不管是不是开源，对，我觉得有些东西应该开源，有些则不该。
cues.en: Open source or not, yeah, I think we should open source some stuff and not other stuff.

cues.zh: 它确实变成了一条宗教式的战线，很难保持细致入微，但我认为细致入微才是正确答案。
cues.en: It does become this religious battle line where nuance is hard to have, but I think nuance is the right answer.

cues.zh: 所以他说：“把你们名字改成 CloseAI，我就撤诉。”我是说，这会不会变成一场围绕名字的表情包大战？
cues.en: So he said, “Change your name to CloseAI and I’ll drop the lawsuit.” I mean is it going to become this battleground in the land of memes about the name?

cues.zh: 我觉得这说明埃隆对这场诉讼是认真的，我觉得这话说出来真是令人震惊。
cues.en: I think that speaks to the seriousness with which Elon means the lawsuit, and that’s like an astonishing thing to say, I think.

cues.zh: 也许我错了你可以纠正我，但我不认为这场诉讼在法律上是严肃的。
cues.en: Maybe correct me if I’m wrong, but I don’t think the lawsuit is legally serious.

cues.zh: 它更多是为了就 AGI 的未来以及目前领先的那家公司表明一个观点。
cues.en: It’s more to make a point about the future of AGI and the company that’s currently leading the way.

cues.zh: 你看，Grok 之前什么都没开源，直到有人指出这有点虚伪，然后他才宣布 Grok 这周会开源一些东西。
cues.en: Look, I mean Grok had not open sourced anything until people pointed out it was a little bit hypocritical and then he announced that Grok will open source things this week.

cues.zh: 我不认为开源与否才是他真正关心的。
cues.en: I don’t think open source versus not is what this is really about for him.

cues.zh: 嗯，我们要聊聊开源，以及不开放的部分。
cues.en: Well, we will talk about open source and not.

cues.zh: 我确实觉得，批评竞争对手也许挺好的。
cues.en: I do think maybe criticizing the competition is great.

cues.zh: 稍微说点难听话，挺好的。
cues.en: Just talking a little shit, that’s great.

cues.zh: 但友好的竞争，对比“我个人讨厌打官司”。
cues.en: But friendly competition versus like, “I personally hate lawsuits.”

cues.zh: 你看，我觉得这整件事对建设者来说很不体面。
cues.en: Look, I think this whole thing is unbecoming of a builder.

cues.zh: 我尊敬埃隆，他是我们这个时代伟大的建设者之一。
cues.en: And I respect Elon as one of the great builders of our time.

cues.zh: 我知道他清楚被黑子攻击是什么滋味，所以他现在这样做，让我格外难过。
cues.en: I know he knows what it’s like to have haters attack him and it makes me extra sad he’s doing it toss.

cues.zh: 是啊，他是史上最伟大的建设者之一，可能是有史以来最伟大的建设者。
cues.en: Yeah, he’s one of the greatest builders of all time, potentially the greatest builder of all time.

cues.zh: 这让我难过。
cues.en: It makes me sad.

cues.zh: 我觉得这也让很多人难过。
cues.en: And I think it makes a lot of people sad.

cues.zh: 有很多人长期以来一直很仰慕他。
cues.en: There’s a lot of people who’ve really looked up to him for a long time.

cues.zh: 我在某次采访里说过，我怀念以前的埃隆，然后我收到好多消息说：“这完全说出了我的感受。”
cues.en: I said in some interview or something that I missed the old Elon and the number of messages I got being like, “That exactly encapsulates how I feel.”

cues.zh: 我觉得他直接赢就好了。
cues.en: I think he should just win.

cues.zh: 他就该让 X Grok 打败 GPT，然后 GPT 再打败 Grok，就是这种竞争，对所有人都是好事。
cues.en: He should just make X Grok beat GPT and then GPT beats Grok and it’s just the competition and it’s beautiful for everybody.

cues.zh: 但关于开源的问题，你觉得有很多公司在琢磨这个想法吗？
cues.en: But on the question of open source, do you think there’s a lot of companies playing with this idea?

cues.zh: 这挺有意思的。
cues.en: It’s quite interesting.

cues.zh: 我会说 Meta 出人意料地在这上面走在了前面，或者说至少在这盘棋里迈出了第一步，真正把模型开源了。
cues.en: I would say Meta surprisingly has led the way on this, or at least took the first step in the game of chess of really open sourcing the model.

cues.zh: 当然它不是最先进的模型，但开源了 Llama，Google 也在试探开源一个更小版本的想法。
cues.en: Of course it’s not the state-of-the-art model, but open sourcing Llama Google is flirting with the idea of open sourcing a smaller version.

cues.zh: 开源的利弊是什么？
cues.en: What are the pros and cons of open sourcing?

cues.zh: 你琢磨过这个想法吗？
cues.en: Have you played around with this idea?

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得开源模型肯定有一席之地，尤其是人们可以在本地运行的小模型，我觉得这方面需求巨大。
cues.en: Yeah, I think there is definitely a place for open source models, particularly smaller models that people can run locally, I think there’s huge demand for.

cues.zh: 我觉得会有一些开源模型，也会有一些闭源模型。
cues.en: I think there will be some open source models, there will be some closed source models.

cues.zh: 这方面和其他生态没什么不同。
cues.en: It won’t be unlike other ecosystems in that way.

cues.zh: 我听了很多播客，都在聊这场诉讼之类的事。
cues.en: I listened to all in podcasts talking about this lawsuit and all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 他们更担心的是从非营利转向这种营利上限的先例。
cues.en: They were more concerned about the precedent of going from nonprofit to this cap for profit.

cues.zh: 这给其他创业公司开了什么先例？
cues.en: What precedent that sets for other startups?

cues.zh: 这是不是——
cues.en: Is that something-

cues.zh: 我会极力劝阻任何想先以非营利起步、之后再加营利部门的创业公司。
cues.en: I would heavily discourage any startup that was thinking about starting as a nonprofit and adding a for-profit arm later.

cues.zh: 我会极力劝阻他们这么做。
cues.en: I’d heavily discourage them from doing that.

cues.zh: 我不认为我们会在这里开先例。
cues.en: I don’t think we’ll set a precedent here.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 所以大多数创业公司应该直接——
cues.en: So most startups should go just-

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: For sure.

cues.zh: 再说——
cues.en: And again-

cues.zh: 如果我们当时知道会发生什么，我们也会那么做。
cues.en: If we knew what was going to happen, we would’ve done that too.

cues.zh: 理论上，如果你在这里运作得漂亮，会有一些税收优惠之类的，但……
cues.en: Well in theory, if you dance beautifully here, there’s some tax incentives or whatever, but…

cues.zh: 我不觉得大多数人是这么看这些事的。
cues.en: I don’t think that’s how most people think about these things.

cues.zh: 如果这样做，创业公司根本省不下多少钱。
cues.en: It’s just not possible to save a lot of money for a startup if you do it this way.

cues.zh: 不行，我觉得有些法规会让这事很难办。
cues.en: No, I think there’s laws that would make that pretty difficult.

cues.zh: 你希望和 Elon 这件事走向何方？
cues.en: Where do you hope this goes with Elon?

cues.zh: 这种紧张关系、这种博弈，你希望它怎样发展？
cues.en: This tension, this dance, what do you hope this?

cues.zh: 如果放到 1 年、2 年、3 年后，你和他私下的关系，比如友谊、良性竞争，诸如此类。
cues.en: If we go 1, 2, 3 years from now, your relationship with him on a personal level too, like friendship, friendly competition, just all this kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 是的，我非常尊重 Elon，我希望未来几年我们能保持友好的关系。
cues.en: Yeah, I really respect Elon and I hope that years in the future we have an amicable relationship.

cues.zh: 是啊，我希望你们这个月就能友好相处，只管竞争、取胜，一起探索这些想法。
cues.en: Yeah, I hope you guys have an amicable relationship this month and just compete and win and explore these ideas together.

cues.zh: 我确实认为人才等方面存在竞争，但应该是良性竞争。
cues.en: I do suppose there’s competition for talent or whatever, but it should be friendly competition.

cues.zh: 就做点酷东西。
cues.en: Just build cool shit.

cues.zh: 而且Elon特别擅长搞酷东西。
cues.en: And Elon is pretty good at building cool shit.

cues.zh: 你也是。
cues.en: So are you.

cues.zh: 说到酷东西，Sora。
cues.en: So speaking of cool shit, Sora.

cues.zh: 我能问的问题有一百万个。
cues.en: There’s like a million questions I could ask.

cues.zh: 首先，它太惊艳了。
cues.en: First of all, it’s amazing.

cues.zh: 在产品层面确实惊艳，在哲学层面也是。
cues.en: It truly is amazing on a product level but also just on a philosophical level.

cues.zh: 那我从技术和哲学角度问一下，你觉得它对世界的理解，相比GPT-4大概多在哪、少在哪？
cues.en: So let me just technical/philosophical ask, what do you think it understands about the world more or less than GPT-4 for example?

cues.zh: 就是基于patch训练的世界模型，对比基于语言token的。
cues.en: The world model when you train on these patches versus language tokens.

cues.zh: 我觉得这些模型对世界模型的理解，比我们大多数人以为的要更多。
cues.en: I think all of these models understand something more about the world model than most of us give them credit for.

cues.zh: 当然也有很明显的地方它们就是不懂或者搞不对，所以很容易盯着弱点看，看穿了那层纱就说：“啊，全是假的。”但并不是全是假的。
cues.en: And because they’re also very clear things they just don’t understand or don’t get right, it’s easy to look at the weaknesses, see through the veil and say, “Ah, this is all fake.” But it’s not all fake.

cues.zh: 有些能用，有些不能用。
cues.en: It’s just some of it works and some of it doesn’t work.

cues.zh: 我记得第一次看 Sora 视频时，看到一个人从某个物体前走过几秒，把它挡住了，然后走开，那个东西还在原地。
cues.en: I remember when I started first watching Sora videos and I would see a person walk in front of something for a few seconds and occlude it and then walk away and the same thing was still there.

cues.zh: 我当时想，“哦，这挺不错的。”还有些例子，底层物理在序列的很多步骤中都表现得非常好，让人觉得“哦，这相当惊艳。”但根本上，这些模型只是在变得更好，而且会持续下去。
cues.en: I was like, “Oh, this is pretty good.” Or there’s examples where the underlying physics looks so well represented over a lot of steps in a sequence, it’s like, “|Oh, this is quite impressive.” But fundamentally, these models are just getting better and that will keep happening.

cues.zh: 如果你看从 DALL·E 1 到 2 到 3 再到 Sora 的发展轨迹，每个版本都有很多人被狠狠打脸，说它做不了这个、做不了那个，再看看现在。
cues.en: If you look at the trajectory from DALL·E 1 to 2 to 3 to Sora, there are a lot of people that were dunked on each version saying it can’t do this, it can’t do that and look at it now.

cues.zh: 你刚才提到的遮挡问题，本质上是要足够好地建模世界的三维物理，才能捕捉到这类现象。
cues.en: Well, the thing you just mentioned is the occlusions is basically modeling the physics of the three-dimensional physics of the world sufficiently well to capture those kinds of things.
Well…

cues.zh: 或者，也许你可以告诉我，为了处理遮挡，世界模型需要做什么？
cues.en: Or yeah, maybe you can tell me, in order to deal with occlusions, what does the world model need to?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以我想说的是，它在处理遮挡方面做得相当好。
cues.en: So what I would say is it’s doing something to deal with occlusions really well.

cues.zh: 但要说它拥有一个强大的底层三维世界模型，那就有点牵强了。
cues.en: What I represent that it has a great underlying 3D model of the world, it’s a little bit more of a stretch.

cues.zh: 但仅靠这类二维训练数据的方法，能走到那一步吗？
cues.en: But can you get there through just these kinds of two-dimensional training data approaches?

cues.zh: 看起来这种方法会走得惊人地远。
cues.en: It looks like this approach is going to go surprisingly far.

cues.zh: 我不想过多猜测它能克服哪些限制、不能克服哪些限制，但……
cues.en: I don’t want to speculate too much about what limits it will surmount and which it won’t, but…

cues.zh: 你观察到这个系统有哪些有趣的局限性？
cues.en: What are some interesting limitations of the system that you’ve seen?

cues.zh: 我是说，你发过一些挺有意思的。
cues.en: I mean there’s been some fun ones you’ve posted.

cues.zh: 各种好玩的东西都有。
cues.en: There’s all kinds of fun.

cues.zh: 我是说，猫会在视频里随机的位置多长出一条腿来。
cues.en: I mean, cat’s sprouting an extra limit at random points in a video.

cues.zh: 你想挑哪个都行，但还是有很多问题，有很多弱点。
cues.en: Pick what you want, but there’s still a lot of problem, there’s a lot of weaknesses.

cues.zh: 你觉得这是方法本身的根本缺陷，还是说只要模型更大、技术细节更好、数据更好或更多，就能解决猫多长腿的问题？
cues.en: Do you think it’s a fundamental flaw of the approach or is it just bigger model or better technical details or better data, more data is going to solve the cat sprouting [inaudible 00:37:19]?

cues.zh: 我觉得两者都对。
cues.en: I would say yes to both.

cues.zh: 我认为这个方法有些地方就是感觉和我们思考、学习的方式不太一样。
cues.en: I think there is something about the approach which just seems to feel different from how we think and learn and whatever.

cues.zh: 而且我觉得随着规模扩大它会变得更好。
cues.en: And then also I think it’ll get better with scale.

cues.zh: 就像我提到的，LLM 有 token，文本 token，而 Sora 有视觉 patch，所以它把所有视觉数据，各种多样的视觉数据，视频和图像，都转换成 patch。
cues.en: Like I mentioned, LLMS have tokens, text tokens, and Sora has visual patches so it converts all visual data, a diverse kinds of visual data videos and images into patches.

cues.zh: 训练是否达到了完全自监督的程度，还是有一些人工标注在进行？
cues.en: Is the training to the degree you can say fully self supervised, there’s some manual labeling going on?

cues.zh: 在这整个过程中，人类参与的程度如何？
cues.en: What’s the involvement of humans in all this?

cues.zh: 我的意思是，不对Sora的具体方法做特别说明，我们在工作中使用了大量的人类数据。
cues.en: I mean without saying anything specific about the Sora approach, we use lots of human data in our work.

cues.zh: 但不是互联网规模的数据？
cues.en: But not internet scale data?

cues.zh: 所以是大量的人力。
cues.en: So lots of humans.

cues.zh: “大量”这个词挺复杂的，Sam。
cues.en: Lots is a complicated word, Sam.

cues.zh: 我认为在这个情况下，“大量”是个恰当的词。
cues.en: I think lots is a fair word in this case.

cues.zh: 因为对我来说，“大量”……听着，我是个内向的人，当我和三个人一起玩的时候，那已经是很多人了。
cues.en: Because to me, “lots”… Listen, I’m an introvert and when I hang out with three people, that’s a lot of people.

cues.zh: 四个人，那就很多了。
cues.en: Four people, that’s a lot.

cues.zh: 但我猜你的意思是超过……
cues.en: But I suppose you mean more than…

cues.en: More than three people work on labeling the data for these models, yeah.

cues.en: Okay.

cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 但根本上，有很多自监督学习。
cues.en: But fundamentally, there’s a lot of self supervised learning.

cues.zh: 因为你技术报告中提到的是互联网规模的数据。
cues.en: Because what you mentioned in the technical report is internet scale data.

cues.zh: 这又是一幅美丽的……就像诗一样。
cues.en: That’s another beautiful… It’s like poetry.

cues.zh: 所以这是大量没有人工标注的数据。
cues.en: So it’s a lot of data that’s not human label.

cues.en: And then the question is, how much data is there on the internet that could be used in this that is conducive to this kind of self supervised way if only we knew the details of the self supervised.

cues.zh: 你有没有考虑过公开更多细节？
cues.en: Have you considered opening it up a little more details?

cues.zh: 你是指专门针对源码？
cues.en: You mean for source specifically?

cues.zh: 专门针对源码。
cues.en: Source specifically.

cues.zh: 因为很有意思的是，LLM的这种魔力现在能否开始转向视觉数据，要做到这一点需要什么？
cues.en: Because it’s so interesting that can the same magic of LLMs now start moving towards visual data and what does that take to do that?

cues.zh: 在我看来答案是肯定的，但我们还有更多工作要做。
cues.en: I mean it looks to me like yes, but we have more work to do.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 危险是什么？
cues.en: What are the dangers?

cues.zh: 你为什么担心发布这个系统？
cues.en: Why are you concerned about releasing the system?

cues.zh: 这可能会带来哪些危险？
cues.en: What are some possible dangers of this?

cues.zh: 说实话，在发布系统之前，我们必须做的一件事就是让它以足够的效率运行，能够支撑人们期望的规模，我不想淡化这一点。
cues.en: I mean frankly speaking, one thing we have to do before releasing the system is just get it to work at a level of efficiency that will deliver the scale people are going to want from this so that I don’t want to downplay that.

cues.zh: 这方面还有大量的工作要做。
cues.en: And there’s still a ton ton of work to do there.

cues.zh: 但你可以想象深度伪造、虚假信息等问题。
cues.en: But you can imagine issues with deepfakes, misinformation.

cues.zh: 我们努力做一家有责任心的公司，慎重考虑我们向世界发布的东西，而且不难想到这件事可能出问题的种种方式。
cues.en: We try to be a thoughtful company about what we put out into the world and it doesn’t take much thought to think about the ways this can go badly.

cues.zh: 这里有很多棘手的问题，你面对的是一个非常艰难的领域。
cues.en: There’s a lot of tough questions here, you’re dealing in a very tough space.

cues.zh: 你认为训练 AI 应该属于、或者确实属于版权法下的合理使用吗？
cues.en: Do you think training AI should be or is fair use under copyright law?

cues.zh: 我认为这个问题背后的问题是：创造有价值数据的人，是否应该以某种方式因数据被使用而获得补偿？我认为答案是肯定的。
cues.en: I think the question behind that question is, do people who create valuable data deserve to have some way that they get compensated for use of it, and that I think the answer is yes.

cues.zh: 我还不知道答案是什么。
cues.en: I don’t know yet what the answer is.

cues.zh: 人们提出了很多不同的方案。
cues.en: People have proposed a lot of different things.

cues.zh: 我们试过一些不同的模型。
cues.en: We’ve tried some different models.

cues.zh: 但比方说，如果我是一个艺术家，A，我希望能选择不让别人用我的风格生成艺术。
cues.en: But if I’m like an artist for example, A, I would like to be able to opt out of people generating art in my style.

cues.zh: B，如果他们真的用我的风格生成了艺术，我希望有某种经济模型与之对应。
cues.en: And B, if they do generate art in my style, I’d like to have some economic model associated with that.

cues.zh: 对，就是从CD到Napster再到Spotify的那种转变。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s that transition from CDs to Napster to Spotify.

cues.zh: 我们得想出某种模式。
cues.en: We have to figure out some kind of model.

cues.zh: 模式会变，但人们得拿到报酬。
cues.en: The model changes but people have got to get paid.

cues.zh: 再往大了说，应该得有某种激励机制，让人类继续做酷炫的事。
cues.en: Well, there should be some kind of incentive if we zoom out even more for humans to keep doing cool shit.

cues.zh: 在我担心的所有事情里，人类会继续做酷炫的事，社会也会找到某种方式来回报它。
cues.en: Of everything I worry about, humans are going to do cool shit and society is going to find some way to reward it.

cues.zh: 这似乎是相当根深蒂固的。
cues.en: That seems pretty hardwired.

cues.zh: 我们想要创造，我们想要有用，我们想以各种方式获得地位。
cues.en: We want to create, we want to be useful, we want to achieve status in whatever way.

cues.zh: 我觉得这不会有什么进展。
cues.en: That’s not going anywhere I don’t think.

cues.zh: 但回报可能不是金钱上的。
cues.en: But the reward might not be monetary financially.

cues.zh: 可能是名声和对其他酷东西的庆祝——
cues.en: It might be fame and celebration of other cool-

cues.zh: 也许是以其他方式获得的财务回报。
cues.en: Maybe financial in some other way.

cues.zh: 再说一次，我认为我们还没有看到经济系统运作方式的最后一次演变。
cues.en: Again, I don’t think we’ve seen the last evolution of how the economic system’s going to work.

cues.zh: 是的，但艺术家和创作者们很担心。
cues.en: Yeah, but artists and creators are worried.

cues.zh: 当他们看到 Sora 时，他们会说：“天哪。”
cues.en: When they see Sora, they’re like, “Holy shit.”

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 摄影出现时，艺术家们也非常担心，然后摄影成为一种新的艺术形式，人们通过拍照赚了很多钱。
cues.en: Artists were also super worried when photography came out and then photography became a new art form and people made a lot of money taking pictures.

cues.zh: 我认为类似的事情会不断发生。
cues.en: I think things like that will keep happening.

cues.zh: 人们会以新的方式使用新工具。
cues.en: People will use the new tools in new ways.

cues.zh: 如果我们只看YouTube之类的平台，你觉得未来五年里，其中有多少内容会是Sora这类AI生成的内容？
cues.en: If we just look on YouTube or something like this, how much of that will be using Sora like AI generated content, do you think, in the next five years?

cues.zh: 人们总在讨论五年内AI会取代多少工作岗位。
cues.en: People talk about how many jobs is AI going to do in five years.

cues.zh: 大家惯常的思维框架是：现有岗位中有多大比例会被某种AI完全替代？
cues.en: The framework that people have is, what percentage of current jobs are just going to be totally replaced by some AI doing the job?

cues.zh: 我的思路不是AI会承担多少比例的工作，而是在不同时间跨度上，AI能完成多少比例的任务。
cues.en: The way I think about it is not what percent of jobs AI will do, but what percent of tasks will AI do on over one time horizon.

cues.zh: 所以，想想经济中所有那些五秒的任务、五分钟的任务、五小时的任务，甚至五天的任务，AI能完成其中多少？
cues.en: So if you think of all of the five-second tasks in the economy, five minute tasks, the five-hour tasks, maybe even the five-day tasks, how many of those can AI do?

cues.zh: 我认为这个问题比“AI能承担多少工作”有趣得多、影响也大得多、重要得多，因为AI是一种工具，它会以越来越高的精细度、在越来越长的时间跨度上、针对越来越多的任务发挥作用，让人们能在更高的抽象层次上运作。
cues.en: I think that’s a way more interesting, impactful, important question than how many jobs AI can do because it is a tool that will work at increasing levels of sophistication and over longer and longer time horizons for more and more tasks and let people operate at a higher level of abstraction.

cues.zh: 所以人们做工作的效率可能会高得多。
cues.en: So maybe people are way more efficient at the job they do.

cues.zh: 到某个时候，这就不只是量变，而是质变了——你能同时装在脑子里的问题种类不一样了。
cues.en: And at some point that’s not just a quantitative change, but it’s a qualitative one too about the kinds of problems you can keep in your head.

cues.zh: 我觉得 YouTube 上的视频也会是这样。
cues.en: I think that for videos on YouTube it’ll be the same.

cues.zh: 很多视频，也许是大多数，制作中会用 AI 工具，但根本上还是由一个人在思考、在组织、在做其中一部分。
cues.en: Many videos, maybe most of them, will use AI tools in the production, but they’ll still be fundamentally driven by a person thinking about it, putting it together, doing parts of it.

cues.zh: 有点像在导演和运营。
cues.en: Sort of directing and running it.

cues.zh: 是啊，太有意思了。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s so interesting.

cues.zh: 我是说这挺吓人的，但想想也很有意思。
cues.en: I mean it’s scary, but it’s interesting to think about.

cues.zh: 我倾向于相信，人就是喜欢看别的人，或者别的真人——
cues.en: I tend to believe that humans like to watch other humans or other human humans-

cues.zh: 人真的很在意其他人。
cues.en: Humans really care about other humans a lot.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 就算有比人更酷、更好的东西，人们也就新鲜两天，然后就又回去看人了。
cues.en: If there’s a cooler thing that’s better than a human, humans care about that for two days and then they go back to humans.

cues.zh: 这似乎是深深植根的东西。
cues.en: That seems very deeply wired.

cues.zh: 就是整个下棋那套，“哦，是啊”，但现在大家继续下棋吧。
cues.en: It’s the whole chess thing, “Oh, yeah,” but now let’s everybody keep playing chess.

cues.zh: 让我们忽略房间里的大象：人类相对AI系统来说下棋真的很差。
cues.en: And let’s ignore the elephant in the room that humans are really bad at chess relative to AI systems.

cues.zh: 我们仍然举办赛跑，而汽车快得多。
cues.en: We still run races and cars are much faster.

cues.zh: 我是说有很多例子。
cues.en: I mean there’s a lot of examples.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 也许它会像Adobe套件里的工具那样，让制作视频变得容易得多之类的。
cues.en: And maybe it’ll just be tooling in the Adobe suite type of way where it can just make videos much easier and all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 听着，我讨厌出现在镜头前。
cues.en: Listen, I hate being in front of the camera.

cues.zh: 如果我能找到不出镜的办法，我会很乐意。
cues.en: If I can figure out a way to not be in front of the camera, I would love it.

cues.zh: 不幸的是，这还需要一段时间。
cues.en: Unfortunately, it’ll take a while.

cues.zh: 生成人脸这块快做到了，但在视频格式里生成特定人物而非泛化人物的面孔很棘手。
cues.en: That generating faces, it is getting there, but generating faces in video format is tricky when it’s specific people versus generic people.

cues.zh: 让我问问你关于 GPT-4 的事。
cues.en: Let me ask you about GPT-4.

cues.zh: 问题太多了。
cues.en: There’s so many questions.

cues.zh: 首先，它同样令人惊叹。
cues.en: First of all, also amazing.

cues.zh: 回头看，GPT-3、GPT-5 和带 ChatGPT 的 GPT-4 大概会是那种历史性的关键时刻。
cues.en: Looking back, it’ll probably be this kind of historic pivotal moment with 3, 5 and 4 which ChatGPT.

cues.zh: 也许第五代才是那个关键时刻。
cues.en: Maybe five will be the pivotal moment.

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 往前看很难说。
cues.en: Hard to say that looking forward.

cues.zh: 我们永远不会知道。
cues.en: We’ll never know.

cues.zh: 未来烦人的地方就在这，很难预测。
cues.en: That’s the annoying thing about the future, it’s hard to predict.

cues.zh: 但对我来说，回头看，GPT-4、ChatGPT 相当惊艳，是历史性的惊艳。
cues.en: But for me, looking back, GPT-4, ChatGPT is pretty damn impressive, historically impressive.

cues.zh: 那么请允许我问一下，对你来说，GPT-4 和 GPT-4 Turbo 最令人印象深刻的能力是什么？

cues.zh: 我觉得它有点烂。
cues.en: I think it kind of sucks.

cues.zh: 典型的人类也是这样，习惯了了不起的东西。
cues.en: Typical human also, gotten used to an awesome thing.

cues.zh: 不，我觉得它很了不起，但相对于我们需要达到的目标和我相信我们会达到的目标，在 GPT-3 那个时候，人们都说：“哦，这太厉害了。
cues.en: No, I think it is an amazing thing, but relative to where we need to get to and where I believe we will get to, at the time of GPT-3, people are like, “Oh, this is amazing.

cues.zh: 这是技术的奇迹。” 确实如此，曾经也是。
cues.en: This is marvel of technology.” And it is, it was.

cues.zh: 但现在我们有了GPT-4，再看GPT-3，你会觉得：“那简直难以想象的糟糕。”我预计5和4之间的差距会和4和3之间一样大，我认为我们的职责是生活在未来几年，并记住我们现在拥有的工具在回顾时会显得有些糟糕，这就是我们确保未来更好的方式。
cues.en: But now we have GPT-4 and look at GPT-3 and you’re like, “That’s unimaginably horrible.” I expect that the delta between 5 and 4 will be the same as between 4 and 3 and I think it is our job to live a few years in the future and remember that the tools we have now are going to kind of suck looking backwards at them and that’s how we make sure the future is better.

cues.zh: GPT-4最糟糕的地方有哪些？
cues.en: What are the most glorious ways in that GPT-4 sucks?

cues.en: Meaning-

cues.en: What are the best things it can do?

cues.zh: 它最擅长做的事情是什么，以及这些最擅长的事情的局限性让你可以说它糟糕，从而给你对未来的灵感和希望？
cues.en: What are the best things it can do and the limits of those best things that allow you to say it sucks, therefore gives you an inspiration and hope for the future?

cues.zh: 我最近更多地把它用作一种头脑风暴伙伴。
cues.en: One thing I’ve been using it for more recently is sort of like a brainstorming partner.

cues.zh: 那里有一丝惊人东西的微光。

cues.en: When people talk about it, what it does, they’re like, “Oh, it helps me code more productively.

cues.en: It helps me write more faster and better.

cues.en: One of the other things that you can see a very small glimpse of is when I can help on longer horizon tasks, break down something in multiple steps, maybe execute some of those steps, search the internet, write code, whatever, put that together.

cues.zh: 成功的时候，虽然不常见，但真的很神奇。
cues.en: When that works, which is not very often, it’s very magical.

cues.zh: 和人类反复迭代交流，对我来说很有效。
cues.en: The iterative back and forth with a human, it works a lot for me.

cues.zh: 你说的“它”是什么意思——
cues.en: What do you mean it-

cues.zh: 和人类反复迭代交流，当它能独立完成一个十步的问题时，这种情况会更常出现。
cues.en: Iterative back and forth to human, it can get more often when it can go do a 10 step problem on its own.

cues.zh: 哦。
cues.en: Oh.

cues.zh: 它做这个并不太常成功，有时候可以。
cues.en: It doesn’t work for that too often, sometimes.

cues.zh: 是加多层抽象，还是说只是顺序执行？
cues.en: Add multiple layers of abstraction or do you mean just sequential?

cues.zh: 两者都有，先拆解，然后用不同层次的抽象把它们组合起来。
cues.en: Both, to break it down and then do things that different layers of abstraction to put them together.

cues.zh: 听着，我不想贬低GPT-4的成就，但也不想夸大它。
cues.en: Look, I don’t want to downplay the accomplishment of GPT-4, but I don’t want to overstate it either.

cues.zh: 我认为我们正处在指数曲线上，不久之后我们回看GPT-4，就会像现在回看GPT-3一样。
cues.en: And I think this point that we are on an exponential curve, we’ll look back relatively soon at GPT-4 like we look back at GPT-3 now.

cues.zh: 话虽如此，ChatGPT是一个转折点，人们开始相信——信心确实在上升，不过在OpenAI内部并非如此。
cues.en: That said, I mean ChatGPT was a transition to where people started to believe there is an uptick of believing, not internally at OpenAI.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: For sure.

cues.zh: 也许这里有信徒，但当你想到——
cues.en: Perhaps there’s believers here, but when you think of-

cues.zh: 从这个意义上说，我确实认为这会是一个时刻，世界上很多人会从怀疑转为相信。
cues.en: And in that sense, I do think it’ll be a moment where a lot of the world went from not believing to believing.

cues.zh: 那更多是关于 ChatGPT 界面。
cues.en: That was more about the ChatGPT interface.

cues.zh: 我说的界面和产品，也包括模型的后训练，以及我们如何调优它，让它对你有帮助、如何更好地使用它，而不只是底层模型本身。
cues.en: And by the interface and product, I also mean the post training of the model and how we tune it to be helpful to you and how to use it than the underlying model itself.

cues.zh: 这些因素各自有多重要？
cues.en: How much of each of those things are important?

cues.zh: 底层模型，以及 RLHF 或类似机制，把它调优得对人类更有吸引力、更有效、更能提升生产力。
cues.en: The underlying model and the RLHF or something of that nature that tunes it to be more compelling to the human, more effective and productive for the human.

cues.zh: 我是说，两者都极其重要，但 RLHF、后训练这一步，从算力角度看，是在基础模型之上做的那一小层包装——尽管工作量巨大——这非常重要，更不用说我们在它周围构建的产品了。
cues.en: I mean they’re both super important, but the RLHF, the post-training step, the little wrapper of things that from a compute perspective, little wrapper of things that we do on top of the base model even though it’s a huge amount of work, that’s really important to say nothing of the product that we build around it.

cues.zh: 从某种意义上说，我们确实得做两件事。
cues.en: In some sense, we did have to do two things.

cues.zh: 我们得先发明底层技术，然后还得想办法把它打造成人们喜爱的产品，这不仅仅是实际的产品工作本身，还涉及另外一整套步骤：如何对齐它、让它变得有用。
cues.en: We had to invent the underlying technology and then we had to figure out how to make it into a product people would love, which is not just about the actual product work itself, but this whole other step of how you align it and make it useful.

cues.zh: 以及如何让规模撑得住，让很多人能同时使用。
cues.en: And how you make the scale work where a lot of people can use it at the same time.

cues.zh: 诸如此类的事情。
cues.en: All that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 还有那个。
cues.en: And that.

cues.zh: 但那是已知的难题。
cues.en: But that was a known difficult thing.

cues.zh: 我们知道必须把它扩展起来。
cues.en: We knew we were going to have to scale it up.

cues.zh: 我们得去做两件前所未有的事，这两件我都得说是相当重大的成就，然后还有很多像扩展规模这样其他公司以前也做过的事。
cues.en: We had to go do two things that had never been done before that were both I would say quite significant achievements and then a lot of things like scaling it up that other companies have had to do before.

cues.zh: 从 GPT-4 到 GPT-4 Turbo，上下文窗口从 8K 到 128K tokens 的提升相比如何？
cues.en: How does the context window of going from 8K to 128K tokens compare from GPT-4 to GPT-4 Turbo?

cues.zh: 大多数人大多数时候并不需要用到128那么长。
cues.en: Most people don’t need all the way to 128 most of the time.

cues.zh: 不过要是畅想遥远的未来，上下文长度会达到几十亿。
cues.en: Although if we dream into the distant future, we’ll have way distant future, we’ll have context length of several billion.

cues.zh: 你会把所有信息、所有历史都喂进去，它就会越来越了解你，那会很棒。
cues.en: You will feed in all of your information, all of your history over time and it’ll just get to know you better and better and that’ll be great.

cues.zh: 但目前人们使用这些模型的方式，并不是这样。
cues.en: For now, the way people use these models, they’re not doing that.

cues.zh: 人们有时会贴一整篇论文，或者代码库的很大一部分，诸如此类，但大多数时候，模型的大多数用法并没有用到长上下文。
cues.en: People sometimes post in a paper or a significant fraction of a code repository, whatever, but most usage of the models is not using the long context most of the time.

cues.zh: 我喜欢这成了你的“我有一个梦想”演讲。
cues.en: I like that this is your “I have a dream” speech.

cues.zh: 总有一天，人们会依据你品格的完整上下文，或者你一生的全部来评判你。
cues.en: One day you’ll be judged by the full context of your character or of your whole lifetime.

cues.zh: 有意思。
cues.en: That’s interesting.

cues.zh: 所以这就是你所期望的扩展的一部分，也就是越来越大的上下文。
cues.en: So that’s part of the expansion that you’re hoping for, is a greater and greater context.

cues.zh: 我曾经看过一个网络视频，具体数字我可能记错了，但大概是比尔·盖茨谈论早期某台计算机的内存容量，可能是64K，也可能是640K，差不多是那个量级。
cues.en: I saw this internet clip once, I’m going to get the numbers wrong, but it was like Bill Gates talking about the amount of memory on some early computer, maybe it was 64K, maybe 640K, something like that.

cues.zh: 其中大部分内存都被屏幕缓冲区占用了。
cues.en: Most of it was used for the screen buffer.

cues.zh: 他就是没法显得真诚。
cues.en: He just couldn’t seem genuine.

cues.zh: 他就是无法想象，这个世界最终会需要计算机拥有几十亿字节甚至几万亿字节的内存。
cues.en: He just couldn’t imagine that the world would eventually need gigabytes of memory in a computer or terabytes of memory in a computer.

cues.zh: 而你总是需要，或者说你总是只需要跟随技术的指数级增长，我们自然会找到如何更好地利用新技术的方法。
cues.en: And you always do, or you always do just need to follow the exponential of technology and we will find out how to use better technology.

cues.zh: 所以我真的无法想象，现在上下文长度有一天会达到十亿级别，那会是什么样子。
cues.en: So I can’t really imagine what it’s like right now for context links to go out to the billion someday.

cues.zh: 他们可能不会真的去那儿，但实际感觉会像那样。
cues.en: And they might not literally go there, but effectively it’ll feel like that.

cues.zh: 但我知道我们会用上它，一旦拥有就真的不想回头了。
cues.en: But I know we’ll use it and really not want to go back once we have it.

cues.zh: 是啊，现在说几十亿，十年后可能都显得很傻，因为那会是数万亿又数万亿。
cues.en: Yeah, even saying billions 10 years from now might seem dumb because it’ll be trillions upon trillions.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 会有某种突破，实际效果感觉就像无限上下文。
cues.en: There’ll be some kind of breakthrough that will effectively feel like infinite context.

cues.zh: 但就算是120，老实说，我也没推到那个程度。
cues.en: But even 120, I have to be honest, I haven’t pushed it to that degree.

cues.zh: 也许是输入整本书或书的一部分，还有论文之类的。
cues.en: Maybe putting in entire books or parts of books and so on, papers.

cues.zh: 你见过GPT-4有哪些有趣的用例？
cues.en: What are some interesting use cases of GPT-4 that you’ve seen?

cues.zh: 我觉得最有意思的不是我们能聊到的某个具体用例，而是那些人——主要是年轻人，但也不全是——他们把GPT-4当作任何知识工作任务的默认起点。
cues.en: The thing that I find most interesting is not any particular use case that we can talk about those, but it’s people who kind of like, this is mostly younger people, but people who use it as their default start for any kind of knowledge work task.

cues.zh: 关键在于它能把很多事情做得相当不错。
cues.en: And it’s the fact that it can do a lot of things reasonably well.

cues.zh: 你可以用 GPT-V，用它帮你写代码、帮你搜索、帮你改论文。
cues.en: You can use GPT-V, you can use it to help you write code, you can use it to help you do search, you can use it to edit a paper.

cues.zh: 对我来说最有趣的是，有些人直接把它当作工作流的起点。
cues.en: The most interesting thing to me is the people who just use it as the start of their workflow.

cues.zh: 我在很多事情上也是这样。
cues.en: I do as well for many things.

cues.zh: 我把它当作读书的伙伴。
cues.en: I use it as a reading partner for reading books.

cues.zh: 它帮我思考，帮我把想法想透，尤其是读经典书的时候。
cues.en: It helps me think, help me think through ideas, especially when the books are classic.

cues.zh: 这些书的论述确实很精彩。
cues.en: So it’s really well written about.

cues.zh: 我发现，在覆盖充分的话题上，它常常比维基百科好得多。
cues.en: I find it often to be significantly better than even Wikipedia on well-covered topics.

cues.zh: 它 somehow 更平衡、更细腻。
cues.en: It’s somehow more balanced and more nuanced.

cues.zh: 也许是我自己的感觉，但它确实比维基百科文章更能激发我深入思考。
cues.en: Or maybe it’s me, but it inspires me to think deeper than a Wikipedia article does.

cues.zh: 我不太确定这到底是什么原因。
cues.en: I’m not exactly sure what that is.

cues.zh: 你提到了这次合作。
cues.en: You mentioned this collaboration.

cues.zh: 我不确定魔力在哪里，是在这里，还是在那里，还是在两者之间。
cues.en: I’m not sure where the magic is, if it’s in here or if it’s in there or if it’s somewhere in between.

cues.zh: 我不确定。
cues.en: I’m not sure.

cues.zh: 但我在用GPT做知识类任务时，有一件事让我担心：通常之后还得做事实核查，比如检查它有没有编造内容。
cues.en: But one of the things that concerns me for knowledge task when I start with GPT is I’ll usually have to do fact checking after, like check that it didn’t come up with fake stuff.

cues.zh: 你怎么发现GPT能编造出听起来非常有说服力的假内容？
cues.en: How do you figure that out that GPT can come up with fake stuff that sounds really convincing?

cues.zh: 那你怎么让它扎根于事实？
cues.en: So how do you ground it in truth?

cues.zh: 这显然是我们非常关注的领域。
cues.en: That’s obviously an area of intense interest for us.

cues.zh: 我觉得接下来的版本会好很多，但我们还得继续努力，今年不可能全部解决。
cues.en: I think it’s going to get a lot better with upcoming versions, but we’ll have to continue to work on it and we’re not going to have it all solved this year.

cues.zh: 可怕的是，随着它变得更好，你会越来越不做事实核查了，对吧？
cues.en: Well the scary thing is, as it gets better, you’ll start not doing the fact checking more and more, right?

cues.zh: 对此我有点矛盾。
cues.en: I’m of two minds about that.

cues.zh: 我觉得人们在使用技术方面，比我们通常认为的要老练得多。
cues.en: I think people are much more sophisticated users of technology than we often give them credit for.

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Sure.

cues.zh: 而且人们似乎真的很清楚，GPT 或这些模型有时会产生幻觉。
cues.en: And people seem to really understand that GPT, any of these models hallucinate some of the time.

cues.zh: 如果事关重大，你就得核实。
cues.en: And if it’s mission-critical, you got to check it.

cues.zh: 只是记者们似乎不明白这一点。
cues.en: Except journalists don’t seem to understand that.

cues.zh: 我见过记者马马虎虎地直接用 GPT-4。
cues.en: I’ve seen journalists half-assedly just using GPT-4.
It’s-

cues.zh: 在我想吐槽记者的长长清单里，这还不是我最主要的批评。
cues.en: Of the long list of things I’d like to dunk on journalists for, this is not my top criticism of them.

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得更大的批评或许是，记者面临的压力和激励是你必须干得特别快，而这就是条捷径。我希望我们的社会能激励——
cues.en: Well, I think the bigger criticism is perhaps the pressures and the incentives of being a journalist is that you have to work really quickly and this is a shortcut.I would love our society to incentivize like-

cues.zh: 我也希望。
cues.en: I would too.

cues.zh: ……比如那种需要花几天几周、并且奖励深度报道的新闻工作。
cues.en: … like a journalistic efforts that take days and weeks and rewards great in depth journalism.

cues.zh: 还有那种平衡呈现的新闻，既赞美又批评，尽管批评才能带来点击，编造也能带来点击，还有完全歪曲事实的标题。
cues.en: Also journalism that present stuff in a balanced way where it’s like celebrates people while criticizing them even though the criticism is the thing that gets clicks and making shit up also gets clicks and headlines that mischaracterized completely.

cues.zh: 我相信有很多人在抨击说：“好吧，那些闹剧大概带来了不少点击。”
cues.en: I’m sure you have a lot of people dunking on, “Well, all that drama probably got a lot of clicks.”

cues.zh: 大概确实如此。
cues.en: Probably did.

cues.zh: 这是人类文明更大的问题，我很想探讨一下。
cues.en: And that’s a bigger problem about human civilization I’d love to see-saw.

cues.zh: 这正是我们应该多庆祝一点的地方。
cues.en: This is where we celebrate a bit more.

cues.zh: 你让 ChatGPT 有了记忆能力。
cues.en: You’ve given ChatGPT the ability to have memories.

cues.zh: 你一直在用它回忆之前的对话。
cues.en: You’ve been playing with that about previous conversations.

cues.zh: 还有关闭记忆的能力。
cues.en: And also the ability to turn off memory.

cues.zh: 有时候我真希望能那样。
cues.en: I wish I could do that sometimes.

cues.zh: 就是根据需要，随时开启和关闭。
cues.en: Just turn on and off, depending.

cues.zh: 我猜有时候酒精能做到这一点，但恐怕效果不太理想。
cues.en: I guess sometimes alcohol can do that, but not optimally I suppose.

cues.zh: 通过探索记住对话、而不是……这个想法，你看到了什么？
cues.en: What have you seen through that, like playing around with that idea of remembering conversations and not…

cues.zh: 我们在这方面的探索还非常早期，但我认为人们想要的，或者至少我自己想要的，是一个能逐渐了解我、随着时间推移对我越来越有用的模型。
cues.en: We’re very early in our explorations here, but I think what people want, or at least what I want for myself, is a model that gets to know me and gets more useful to me over time.

cues.zh: 这是一项早期探索。
cues.en: This is an early exploration.

cues.zh: 我觉得还有很多其他事情要做，但那是我们希望前进的方向。
cues.en: I think there’s a lot of other things to do, but that’s where we’d like to head.

cues.zh: 你希望使用一个模型，在你的人生历程中，或者说使用一个系统——那会是很多个模型——随着你的人生推进，它变得越来越好。
cues.en: You’d like to use a model, and over the course of your life or use a system, it’d be many models, and over the course of your life it gets better and better.

cues.zh: 因为现在它更像是记住一些零碎的事实和偏好之类的。
cues.en: Because right now it’s more like remembering little factoids and preferences and so on.

cues.zh: 你不希望GPT记住你十一月经历的所有破事和那些抓马，然后你就能——
cues.en: Don’t you want GPT to remember all the shit you went through in November and all the drama and then you can-

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 因为现在你显然有点在刻意回避它。
cues.en: Because right now you’re clearly blocking it out a little bit.

cues.zh: 不只是我想让它记住那些。
cues.en: It’s not just that I want it to remember that.

cues.zh: 我想让它整合那些经验教训，并在未来提醒我该怎么做才不同，或者该提防什么。
cues.en: I want it to integrate the lessons of that and remind me in the future what to do differently or what to watch out for.

cues.zh: 我们一生中都会不同程度地从经验中获益，我希望我的AI agent也能随这些经验一起成长。
cues.en: We all gain from experience over the course of our lives in varying degrees, and I’d like my AI agent to gain with that experience too.

cues.zh: 所以如果我们回过头去，设想有万亿级的上下文长度，如果我能把一生中跟任何人进行过的每一次对话都放进去，如果每次提问时，所有邮件的输入输出都能进入上下文窗口，我觉得那会相当酷。
cues.en: So if we go back and let ourselves imagine that trillions and trillions of context length, if I can put every conversation I’ve ever had with anybody in my life in there, if I can have all of my emails input out, all of my input output in the context window every time I ask a question, that’d be pretty cool I think.

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得那会很酷。
cues.en: Yeah, I think that would be very cool.

cues.zh: 人们有时听到这个会担心隐私问题。
cues.en: People sometimes will hear that and be concerned about privacy.

cues.zh: 你怎么看这方面——AI 越高效，就越能整合你所有的经历和所有数据，给你建议？
cues.en: What do you think about that aspect of it, the more effective the AI becomes that really integrating all the experiences and all the data that happened to you and give you advice?

cues.zh: 我觉得正确的答案就是让用户选择。
cues.en: I think the right answer there is just user choice.

cues.zh: 任何我想从我的 AI 助手中抹去的记录，我都希望能删掉。
cues.en: Anything I want stricken from the record from my AI agent, I want to be able to take out.

cues.zh: 如果我不想记住任何东西，我也希望能做到。
cues.en: If I don’t want to remember anything, I want that too.

cues.zh: 你和我对于我们自己 AI 的隐私与实用性权衡点可能有不同看法——
cues.en: You and I may have different opinions about where on that privacy utility trade off for our own AI-

cues.zh: ……对于 OpenAI 在隐私与实用性权衡上的看法，这完全没问题。
cues.en: …opinions about where on that privacy/utility trade-off for OpenAI going to be, which is totally fine.

cues.zh: 但我认为答案很简单，就是让用户选择。
cues.en: But I think the answer is just really easy user choice.

cues.zh: 但公司应该在用户选择方面保持一定程度的透明度。
cues.en: But there should be some high level of transparency from a company about the user choice.

cues.zh: 因为过去有些公司在这件事上挺不透明的，“呃，我们就默认在收集你的所有数据了。
cues.en: Because sometimes companies in the past have been kind of shady about, “Eh, it’s kind of presumed that we’re collecting all your data.

cues.zh: 我们是有正当理由的，比如用于广告等等。”但对于具体细节并不透明。
cues.en: We’re using it for a good reason, for advertisement and so on.” But there’s not a transparency about the details of that.

cues.zh: 确实如此。
cues.en: That’s totally true.

cues.zh: 你之前提到我在回避十一月的事。
cues.en: You mentioned earlier that I’m blocking out the November stuff.

cues.zh: 逗你玩的。
cues.en: Just teasing you.

cues.zh: 我是说，我觉得那件事非常创伤性，确实让我很长一段时间动弹不得。
cues.en: Well, I mean, I think it was a very traumatic thing and it did immobilize me for a long period of time.

cues.zh: 最难的工作绝对是那段时间还得继续干活，因为我得试着回到这里把碎片拼起来，而当时我还处在震惊和痛苦中，根本没人真正在意这些。
cues.en: Definitely the hardest work thing I’ve had to do was just keep working that period, because I had to try to come back in here and put the pieces together while I was just in shock and pain, and nobody really cares about that.

cues.zh: 我是说，团队给了我一次机会，而我当时的状态并不在正常水平。
cues.en: I mean, the team gave me a pass and I was not working at my normal level.

cues.zh: 但有一段时间，要同时兼顾两边真的很难。
cues.en: But there was a period where it was really hard to have to do both.

cues.zh: 但有一天早上我醒来，我心想：“这件事发生在我身上太糟糕了。
cues.en: But I kind of woke up one morning, and I was like, “This was a horrible thing that happened to me.

cues.zh: 我觉得我可以永远把自己当成受害者，或者我可以说，这是我这辈子最重要的作品，我需要回到它上面去。”这并不意味着我已经压抑了它，因为有时我半夜醒来还会想到它，但我确实觉得有义务继续向前走。
cues.en: I think I could just feel like a victim forever, or I can say this is the most important work I’ll ever touch in my life and I need to get back to it.” And it doesn’t mean that I’ve repressed it, because sometimes I wake up in the middle of the night thinking about it, but I do feel an obligation to keep moving forward.

cues.zh: 嗯，说得真美，但里面可能还有些残留的东西。
