cues.en: Well, that’s beautifully said, but there could be some lingering stuff in there.

cues.zh: 比如，我会担心的是你提到的那种信任问题，就是对人心存戒备，而不是信任所有人或大多数人，比如相信自己的直觉。
cues.en: Like, what I would be concerned about is that trust thing that you mentioned, that being paranoid about people as opposed to just trusting everybody or most people, like using your gut.

cues.zh: 这确实是种微妙的平衡。
cues.en: It’s a tricky dance.

cues.zh: 确实如此。
cues.en: For sure.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，因为我在业余时间的探索中看到过，我一直在深入研究泽连斯基政府和普京政府，以及战时那种高压环境下的动态。
cues.en: I mean, because I’ve seen in my part-time explorations, I’ve been diving deeply into the Zelenskyy administration and the Putin administration and the dynamics there in wartime in a very highly stressful environment.

cues.zh: 结果就是互不信任，双方都把自己孤立起来，然后开始看不清世界。
cues.en: And what happens is distrust, and you isolate yourself, both, and you start to not see the world clearly.

cues.zh: 这是人类共有的担忧。
cues.en: And that’s a human concern.

cues.zh: 你似乎从容应对了这一切，学到了好的经验，感受到了爱，并让爱给你力量，这很棒，但那种影响仍可能 lingering。
cues.en: You seem to have taken it in stride and kind of learned the good lessons and felt the love and let the love energize you, which is great, but still can linger in there.

cues.zh: 有几个问题我很想问你，关于你对 GPT 能做什么、不能做什么的直觉。
cues.en: There’s just some questions I would love to ask, your intuition about what’s GPT able to do and not.

cues.zh: 它为自己生成的每个 token 分配的计算量大致相同。
cues.en: So it’s allocating approximately the same amount of compute for each token it generates.

cues.zh: 这种方法里有没有空间容纳更慢的思考、顺序思考？
cues.en: Is there room there in this kind of approach to slower thinking, sequential thinking?

cues.zh: 我认为这类思考会有一个新的范式。
cues.en: I think there will be a new paradigm for that kind of thinking.

cues.zh: 它在架构上会类似于我们现在看到的 LLM 吗？
cues.en: Will it be similar architecturally as what we’re seeing now with LLMs?

cues.zh: 它是 LLM 之上的一层吗？
cues.en: Is it a layer on top of LLMs?

cues.zh: 我能想象出很多实现方式。
cues.en: I can imagine many ways to implement that.

cues.zh: 我觉得这不如你真正想问的问题重要，那就是：我们是否需要一种更慢的思考方式，让答案不必……我想从精神层面说，你希望 AI 能对更难的问题思考得更深入，对更简单的问题回答得更快。
cues.en: I think that’s less important than the question you were getting at, which is, do we need a way to do a slower kind of thinking, where the answer doesn’t have to get… I guess spiritually you could say that you want an AI to be able to think harder about a harder problem and answer more quickly about an easier problem.

cues.zh: 我认为那会很重要。
cues.en: And I think that will be important.

cues.zh: 这就像人类本来就有的思考方式，你应该能够深入思考？
cues.en: Is that like a human thought that we just have and you should be able to think hard?

cues.zh: 这个直觉错了吗？
cues.en: Is that wrong intuition?

cues.zh: 我觉得这个直觉挺合理。
cues.en: I suspect that’s a reasonable intuition.

cues.zh: 有意思。
cues.en: Interesting.

cues.zh: 所以等GPT发展到GPT-7，也不可能瞬间就看到“这是费马大定理的证明”？
cues.en: So it’s not possible once the GPT gets like GPT-7, would just instantaneously be able to see, “Here’s the proof of Fermat’s Theorem”?

cues.zh: 在我看来，你会希望把更多算力分配给更难的问题。
cues.en: It seems to me like you want to be able to allocate more compute to harder problems.

cues.zh: 在我看来，如果你让这样的系统去“证明费马大定理”，而不是问“今天几号？”，除非它已经知道并记住了证明的答案，假设它得自己去推导出来，那似乎会需要更多算力。
cues.en: It seems to me that if you ask a system like that, “Prove Fermat’s Last Theorem,” versus, “What’s today’s date?,” unless it already knew and and had memorized the answer to the proof, assuming it’s got to go figure that out, seems like that will take more compute.

cues.zh: 但它看起来基本上就像一个LLM在自言自语，那种感觉？
cues.en: But can it look like basically an LLM talking to itself, that kind of thing?

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 我是说，你能想象有很多东西都可能行得通。
cues.en: I mean, there’s a lot of things that you could imagine working.

cues.zh: 我们不知道正确或最好的做法会是什么。
cues.en: What the right or the best way to do that will be, we don’t know.

cues.zh: 这确实让我想到 Q* 背后的神秘传说。
cues.en: This does make me think of the mysterious lore behind Q*.

cues.zh: 这个神秘的 Q* 项目是什么？
cues.en: What’s this mysterious Q* project?

cues.zh: 它也在同一个核设施里吗？
cues.en: Is it also in the same nuclear facility?

cues.zh: 没有什么核设施。
cues.en: There is no nuclear facility.

cues.zh: 嗯哼。
cues.en: Mm-hmm.

cues.zh: 有核设施的人总是这么说。
cues.en: That’s what a person with a nuclear facility always says.

cues.zh: 我倒真想有个秘密核设施。
cues.en: I would love to have a secret nuclear facility.

cues.zh: 真没有。
cues.en: There isn’t one.

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 也许有一天吧。
cues.en: Maybe someday.

cues.zh: 有一天？
cues.en: Someday?

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 人总可以做梦嘛。
cues.en: One can dream.

cues.zh: OpenAI 可不是个擅长保密的公司。
cues.en: OpenAI is not a good company at keeping secrets.

cues.zh: 那倒挺好。
cues.en: It would be nice.

cues.zh: 我们一直被大量泄密困扰，要是能有这么个东西就好了。
cues.en: We’re like, been plagued by a lot of leaks, and it would be nice if we were able to have something like that.

cues.zh: 你能谈谈 Q* 是什么吗？
cues.en: Can you speak to what Q* is?

cues.zh: 我们还没准备好谈这个。
cues.en: We are not ready to talk about that.

cues.zh: 看吧，但这样的回答意味着确实有东西可谈。
cues.en: See, but an answer like that means there’s something to talk about.

cues.zh: 这很神秘，Sam。
cues.en: It’s very mysterious, Sam.

cues.zh: 我是说，我们做各种研究。
cues.en: I mean, we work on all kinds of research.

cues.zh: 我们早就说过，我们认为这些系统有更好的推理能力是我们想要追求的重要方向。
cues.en: We have said for a while that we think better reasoning in these systems is an important direction that we’d like to pursue.

cues.zh: 我们还没破解这个难题。
cues.en: We haven’t cracked the code yet.

cues.zh: 我们对此非常感兴趣。
cues.en: We’re very interested in it.

cues.zh: 会不会有那样的时刻，Q* 或其他什么，出现类似 ChatGPT 那样的飞跃，让你觉得……
cues.en: Is there going to be moments, Q* or otherwise, where there’s going to be leaps similar to ChatGPT, where you’re like…

cues.zh: 这是个好问题。
cues.en: That’s a good question.

cues.zh: 我怎么看这件事？
cues.en: What do I think about that?

cues.zh: 很有意思。
cues.en: It’s interesting.

cues.zh: 对我来说，一切感觉都挺连续的。
cues.en: To me, it all feels pretty continuous.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 你说的这算是个主题，就是你基本上是在沿着一条指数曲线逐步上升。
cues.en: This is kind of a theme that you’re saying, is you’re basically gradually going up an exponential slope.

cues.zh: 但从局外人的角度看，从我旁观的角度看，确实感觉有飞跃。
cues.en: But from an outsider’s perspective, from me just watching, it does feel like there’s leaps.

cues.zh: 但对你来说，没有？
cues.en: But to you, there isn’t?

cues.zh: 我确实在想我们是不是应该……我们这样部署的部分原因，我们称之为迭代部署，而不是秘密构建直到一路做到 GPT-5，我们决定公开讨论 GPT-1、2、3 和 4。
cues.en: I do wonder if we should have… So part of the reason that we deploy the way we do, we call it iterative deployment, rather than go build in secret until we got all the way to GPT-5, we decided to talk about GPT-1, 2, 3, and 4.

cues.zh: 我觉得部分原因是，AI和意外不太搭。
cues.en: And part of the reason there is I think AI and surprise don’t go together.

cues.zh: 而且这个世界、人们、机构，不管你怎么称呼它，都需要时间来适应和思考这些事情。
cues.en: And also the world, people, institutions, whatever you want to call it, need time to adapt and think about these things.

cues.zh: 我认为OpenAI做得最好的事情之一就是这个策略，让全世界关注进展，认真对待AGI，思考我们希望在被迫仓促决策之前建立什么样的系统和结构以及治理。
cues.en: And I think one of the best things that OpenAI has done is this strategy, and we get the world to pay attention to the progress, to take AGI seriously, to think about what systems and structures and governance we want in place before we’re under the gun and have to make a rush decision.

cues.zh: 我觉得这真的很好。
cues.en: I think that’s really good.

cues.zh: 但像你和其他人仍然觉得存在这些跳跃，这让我觉得也许我们应该更加迭代地发布。
cues.en: But the fact that people like you and others say you still feel like there are these leaps makes me think that maybe we should be doing our releasing even more iteratively.

cues.zh: 我不知道那意味着什么，我也没有现成的答案，但我们的目标不是给世界带来冲击性的更新。
cues.en: And I don’t know what that would mean, I don’t have an answer ready to go, but our goal is not to have shock updates to the world.

cues.zh: 恰恰相反。
cues.en: The opposite.

cues.zh: 嗯，确实。
cues.en: Yeah, for sure.

cues.zh: 更迭代式会非常棒。
cues.en: More iterative would be amazing.

cues.zh: 我觉得这对所有人来说都很美好。
cues.en: I think that’s just beautiful for everybody.

cues.zh: 但这正是我们想做的，这是我们明确的策略，可我觉得我们不知怎么地没做到点子上。
cues.en: But that’s what we’re trying to do, that’s our stated strategy, and I think we’re somehow missing the mark.

cues.zh: 所以也许我们该考虑用另一种方式发布 GPT-5 之类的。
cues.en: So maybe we should think about releasing GPT-5 in a different way or something like that.

cues.zh: 但人们往往喜欢庆祝，人们会庆祝生日。
cues.en: But people tend to like to celebrate, people celebrate birthdays.

cues.zh: 不知道你认不认识人类，但他们确实有这种里程碑式的东西。
cues.en: I don’t know if you know humans, but they kind of have these milestones and those things.

cues.zh: 我确实认识一些人类。
cues.en: I do know some humans.

cues.zh: 人们确实喜欢里程碑。
cues.en: People do like milestones.

cues.zh: 我完全理解。
cues.en: I totally get that.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们也喜欢里程碑。
cues.en: I think we like milestones too.

cues.zh: 在这件事上宣布胜利，然后开始下一件事，挺有意思的。
cues.en: It’s fun to declare victory on this one and go start the next thing.

cues.zh: 但是啊，我感觉我们不知怎么地把这事搞得有点不对。
cues.en: But yeah, I feel like we’re somehow getting this a little bit wrong.

cues.zh: 那GPT-5到底什么时候出？
cues.en: So when is GPT-5 coming out again?

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 这是实话。
cues.en: That’s the honest answer.

cues.zh: 哦，这是实话。
cues.en: Oh, that’s the honest answer.

cues.zh: 如果是今年，眨两下眼。
cues.en: Blink twice if it’s this year.

cues.zh: 我们今年会发布一个惊艳的新模型。
cues.en: We will release an amazing new model this year.

cues.zh: 我不知道我们会怎么命名它。
cues.en: I don’t know what we’ll call it.

cues.zh: 所以这就回到一个问题：我们该以什么方式发布它？
cues.en: So that goes to the question of, what’s the way we release this thing?

cues.zh: 未来几个月我们会发布很多不同的东西。
cues.en: We’ll release in the coming months many different things.

cues.zh: 我觉得那会很酷。
cues.en: I think that’d be very cool.

cues.zh: 我觉得，在讨论一个叫GPT-5、或者不叫GPT-5、或者比预期稍差或稍好的模型之前，我们还有很多其他重要的东西要先发布。
cues.en: I think before we talk about a GPT-5-like model called that, or not called that, or a little bit worse or a little bit better than what you’d expect from a GPT-5, I think we have a lot of other important things to release first.

cues.zh: 我不知道该对GPT-5抱什么期待。
cues.en: I don’t know what to expect from GPT-5.

cues.zh: 你让我又紧张又兴奋。
cues.en: You’re making me nervous and excited.

cues.zh: 不管它最终叫什么——我们就叫它GPT-5吧——要克服的最大挑战和瓶颈有哪些？
cues.en: What are some of the biggest challenges and bottlenecks to overcome for whatever it ends up being called, but let’s call it GPT-5?

cues.zh: 问得很有意思。
cues.en: Just interesting to ask.

cues.zh: 是在算力方面吗？
cues.en: Is it on the compute side?

cues.zh: 是在技术方面吗？
cues.en: Is it on the technical side?

cues.zh: 一直都是所有这些因素。
cues.en: It’s always all of these.

cues.zh: 你知道，最大的突破口是什么吗？
cues.en: You know, what’s the one big unlock?

cues.zh: 是更大的计算机吗？
cues.en: Is it a bigger computer?

cues.zh: 是新的秘密吗？
cues.en: Is it a new secret?

cues.zh: 还是别的什么？
cues.en: Is it something else?

cues.zh: 是所有这些因素加在一起。
cues.en: It’s all of these things together.

cues.zh: 我认为 OpenAI 做得特别好的一点……这其实是 Ilya 的原话，我可能会说走样，但大意是：“我们把 200 个中等规模的东西相乘，变成一个巨大的东西。”
cues.en: The thing that OpenAI, I think, does really well… This is actually an original Ilya quote that I’m going to butcher, but it’s something like, “We multiply 200 medium-sized things together into one giant thing.”

cues.zh: 所以是这种分布式的持续创新在发生？
cues.en: So there’s this distributed constant innovation happening?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以即使在技术层面也是如此？
cues.en: So even on the technical side?

cues.zh: 尤其是在技术层面。
cues.en: Especially on the technical side.

cues.zh: 所以连细节方法也是？
cues.en: So even detailed approaches?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 比如你深入每个细节方面……这在不同的、分散的团队之间是怎么运作的？
cues.en: Like you do detailed aspects of every… How does that work with different, disparate teams and so on?

cues.zh: 中等规模的部分是怎么组成一个完整的巨型Transformer的？
cues.en: How do the medium-sized things become one whole giant Transformer?

cues.zh: 有少数人必须考虑如何把整体拼起来，但很多人会尽量把大部分图景记在脑子里。
cues.en: There’s a few people who have to think about putting the whole thing together, but a lot of people try to keep most of the picture in their head.

cues.zh: 哦，就像各个团队、各个贡献者都尽量把握更大的图景？
cues.en: Oh, like the individual teams, individual contributors try to keep the bigger picture?

cues.zh: 从高层来说，是的。
cues.en: At a high level, yeah.

cues.zh: 你当然不会确切知道每个部分怎么运作，但我普遍相信，有时拉远视角、看整张地图是很有用的。
cues.en: You don’t know exactly how every piece works, of course, but one thing I generally believe is that it’s sometimes useful to zoom out and look at the entire map.

cues.zh: 我觉得这对技术问题成立，对商业创新也成立。
cues.en: And I think this is true for a technical problem, I think this is true for innovating in business.

cues.zh: 但事情会以出人意料的方式拼合起来，而对整体图景有所理解，即便大多数时候你都在某个领域的细节里干活，也会带来意想不到的洞见。
cues.en: But things come together in surprising ways, and having an understanding of that whole picture, even if most of the time you’re operating in the weeds in one area, pays off with surprising insights.

cues.zh: 其实，我以前拥有的一样特别有价值的东西，就是我对科技行业所有或大部分前沿领域有一张清晰的认知地图。
cues.en: In fact, one of the things that I used to have and was super valuable was I used to have a good map of all or most of the frontiers in the tech industry.

cues.zh: 有时我能看到这些联系或新出现的可能性，而如果我仅仅深耕于一个领域，就无法产生这样的想法，因为我不会有全部的数据。
cues.en: And I could sometimes see these connections or new things that were possible that if I were only deep in one area, I wouldn’t be able to have the idea for because I wouldn’t have all the data.

cues.zh: 而我现在已经不太有这种能力了。
cues.en: And I don’t really have that much anymore.

cues.zh: 我现在非常专注深入。
cues.en: I’m super deep now.

cues.zh: 但我知道这是很有价值的东西。
cues.en: But I know that it’s a valuable thing.

cues.zh: 你已经不是以前的你了，Sam。
cues.en: You’re not the man you used to be, Sam.

cues.zh: 现在的工作和我以前的工作非常不同。
cues.en: Very different job now than what I used to have.

cues.zh: 说到拉远视角，让我们拉远来看另一件你提到的既俏皮又深刻的事情。
cues.en: Speaking of zooming out, let’s zoom out to another cheeky thing, but profound thing, perhaps, that you said.

cues.zh: 你发推说需要7万亿美元。
cues.en: You tweeted about needing $7 trillion.

cues.zh: 我没有发推说那个。
cues.en: I did not tweet about that.

cues.zh: 我从没说过“我们要融资7万亿美元”之类的话。
cues.en: I never said, like, “We’re raising $7 trillion,” blah blah blah.

cues.zh: 哦，那是别人说的？
cues.en: Oh, that’s somebody else?

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 哦，但你说过“管他呢，也许八万亿”，我记得是这样？
cues.en: Oh, but you said, “Fuck it, maybe eight,” I think?

cues.zh: 好吧，我在那儿玩了个梗，因为世界上有错误信息。
cues.en: Okay, I meme once there’s misinformation out in the world.

cues.zh: 哦，你玩梗。
cues.en: Oh, you meme.

cues.zh: 但那些错误信息背后可能有一点洞察的基础。
cues.en: But misinformation may have a foundation of insight there.

cues.zh: 听着，我认为算力会成为未来的货币。
cues.en: Look, I think compute is going to be the currency of the future.

cues.zh: 我认为它可能会是世界上最有价值的大宗商品，我们应该大力投资，制造多得多的算力。
cues.en: I think it will be maybe the most precious commodity in the world, and I think we should be investing heavily to make a lot more compute.

cues.zh: 我认为算力会是一个不寻常的市场。
cues.en: Compute, I think it’s going to be an unusual market.

cues.zh: 人们会想到手机芯片之类的市场。
cues.en: People think about the market for chips for mobile phones or something like that.

cues.zh: 你可以说，好吧，世界上有80亿人，也许其中70亿人有手机，也许60亿，就这么说吧。
cues.en: And you can say that, okay, there’s 8 billion people in the world, maybe 7 billion of them have phones, maybe 6 billion, let’s say.

cues.zh: 他们每两年升级一次，所以每年智能手机系统级芯片的市场是30亿颗。
cues.en: They upgrade every two years, so the market per year is 3 billion system-on-chip for smartphones.

cues.zh: 就算你做300亿颗，手机销量也不会翻十倍，因为大多数人只有一部手机。
cues.en: And if you make 30 billion, you will not sell 10 times as many phones, because most people have one phone.

cues.zh: 但算力不一样。
cues.en: But compute is different.

cues.zh: 智能会更像能源之类的东西，我觉得唯一有意义的讨论方式是：在价格X下，世界会用这么多算力；在价格Y下，世界会用这么多算力。
cues.en: Intelligence is going to be more like energy or something like that, where the only thing that I think makes sense to talk about is, at price X, the world will use this much compute, and at price Y, the world will use this much compute.

cues.zh: 因为如果它真的很便宜，我会让它整天读我的邮件，给我建议该思考什么、做什么，还会试着攻克癌症；如果它真的很贵，也许我只会用它，或者我们只会用它，来试着攻克癌症。
cues.en: Because if it’s really cheap, I’ll have it reading my email all day, giving me suggestions about what I maybe should think about or work on, and trying to cure cancer, and if it’s really expensive, maybe I’ll only use it, or we’ll only use it, to try to cure cancer.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，世界将会需要海量的算力。
cues.en: So I think the world is going to want a tremendous amount of compute.

cues.zh: 而这其中有很多部分都很难。
cues.en: And there’s a lot of parts of that that are hard.

cues.zh: 能源是最难的部分，建数据中心也很难，供应链很难，当然，造出足够多的芯片也很难。
cues.en: Energy is the hardest part, building data centers is also hard, the supply chain is hard, and then of course, fabricating enough chips is hard.

cues.zh: 但这似乎就是事物发展的方向。
cues.en: But this seems to be where things are going.

cues.zh: 我们将需要的算力规模，现在简直难以想象。
cues.en: We’re going to want an amount of compute that’s just hard to reason about right now.

cues.zh: 能源难题怎么解决？
cues.en: How do you solve the energy puzzle?

cues.zh: 核能——
cues.en: Nuclear-

cues.zh: 这就是我的信念。
cues.en: That’s what I believe.

cues.zh: ……聚变？
cues.en: …fusion?

cues.zh: 这就是我的信念。
cues.en: That’s what I believe.

cues.zh: 核聚变？
cues.en: Nuclear fusion?

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 谁来攻克它？
cues.en: Who’s going to solve that?

cues.zh: 我认为 Helion 做得最好，但我很高兴现在聚变领域有了一场竞赛。
cues.en: I think Helion’s doing the best work, but I’m happy there’s a race for fusion right now.

cues.zh: 核裂变，我觉得也相当了不起，我希望全世界能重新拥抱它。
cues.en: Nuclear fission, I think, is also quite amazing, and I hope as a world we can re-embrace that.

cues.zh: 这段历史真让人难过，希望我们能以有意义的方式回到正轨。
cues.en: It’s really sad to me how the history of that went, and hope we get back to it in a meaningful way.

cues.zh: 所以对你来说，谜题的一部分是核裂变？
cues.en: So to you, part of the puzzle is nuclear fission?

cues.zh: 就像我们目前拥有的核反应堆那样？
cues.en: Like nuclear reactors as we currently have them?

cues.zh: 很多人因为切尔诺贝利之类的事件而非常恐惧？
cues.en: And a lot of people are terrified because of Chernobyl and so on?

cues.zh: 嗯，我认为我们应该建造新的反应堆。
cues.en: Well, I think we should make new reactors.

cues.zh: 我觉得很遗憾，这个行业基本上停滞了。
cues.en: I think it’s just a shame that industry kind of ground to a halt.

cues.zh: 你就用大规模恐慌来解释这种停滞？
cues.en: And just mass hysteria is how you explain the halt?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我不知道你熟不熟悉人类，但这就是危险之一。
cues.en: I don’t know if you know humans, but that’s one of the dangers.

cues.zh: 这是核裂变的安全威胁之一，人类似乎真的很害怕它。
cues.en: That’s one of the security threats for nuclear fission, is humans seem to be really afraid of it.

cues.zh: 这是我们必须纳入考量的事情，所以我们必须赢得人们的支持，向他们展示它有多安全。
cues.en: And that’s something we’ll have to incorporate into the calculus of it, so we have to kind of win people over and to show how safe it is.

cues.zh: 我也为 AI 担心这一点。
cues.en: I worry about that for AI.

cues.zh: 我觉得 AI 有些事会以戏剧性的方式出错。
cues.en: I think some things are going to go theatrically wrong with AI.

cues.zh: 我不知道我最终被枪击的概率是多少，但不是零。
cues.en: I don’t know what the percent chance is that I eventually get shot, but it’s not zero.

cues.zh: 哦，就像我们想阻止这件事——
cues.en: Oh, like we want to stop this from-

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 你怎么降低它的戏剧性？
cues.en: How do you decrease the theatrical nature of it?

cues.zh: 我已经开始听到一些风声了，因为我确实跟政治光谱两边的人都聊过，听到风声说这事会被政治化。
cues.en: I’m already starting to hear rumblings, because I do talk to people on both sides of the political spectrum, hear rumblings where it’s going to be politicized.

cues.zh: AI 会被政治化，这让我很担心，因为那样的话，可能右派反对 AI，左派支持 AI，说它会帮助人们，或者不管叙事和说法是什么，这真的让我担心。
cues.en: AI is going to be politicized, which really worries me, because then it’s like maybe the right is against AI and the left is for AI because it’s going to help the people, or whatever the narrative and the formulation is, that really worries me.

cues.zh: 然后它的戏剧性就能被充分利用了。
cues.en: And then the theatrical nature of it can be leveraged fully.

cues.zh: 你怎么应对这个问题？
cues.en: How do you fight that?

cues.zh: 我觉得它会被卷入左右派之争。
cues.en: I think it will get caught up in left versus right wars.

cues.zh: 我不确定那具体会是什么样，但我觉得任何有重大影响的事都会这样，很不幸。
cues.en: I don’t know exactly what that’s going to look like, but I think that’s just what happens with anything of consequence, unfortunately.

cues.zh: 我说的戏剧性风险，更多是指AI带来的好结果会远远多于坏结果，我相信如此，但它确实会有坏结果，而且有些坏结果虽然糟糕，却不够戏剧化。
cues.en: What I meant more about theatrical risks is AI’s going to have, I believe, tremendously more good consequences than bad ones, but it is going to have bad ones, and there’ll be some bad ones that are bad but not theatrical.

cues.zh: 比如，死于空气污染的人比死于核反应堆的人多得多。
cues.en: A lot more people have died of air pollution than nuclear reactors, for example.

cues.zh: 但大多数人更担心住在核反应堆旁边，而不是煤电厂旁边。
cues.en: But most people worry more about living next to a nuclear reactor than a coal plant.

cues.zh: 但我们天性中的某种东西是，尽管我们要面对许多不同种类的风险，那些能成为电影高潮场景的风险，在我们心中的分量远远大于那些长期缓慢累积、非常糟糕的风险。
cues.en: But something about the way we’re wired is that although there’s many different kinds of risks we have to confront, the ones that make a good climax scene of a movie carry much more weight with us than the ones that are very bad over a long period of time but on a slow burn.

cues.zh: 所以这就是为什么真相很重要，希望AI能帮我们看清事物的真相，保持平衡，理解世界上事物真正的风险和真正的危险。
cues.en: Well, that’s why truth matters, and hopefully AI can help us see the truth of things, to have balance, to understand what are the actual risks, what are the actual dangers of things in the world.

cues.zh: 在这个领域竞争，与Google、Meta、xAI等公司竞争，有什么利弊？
cues.en: What are the pros and cons of the competition in the space and competing with Google, Meta, xAI, and others?

cues.zh: 我想我对此有一个相当直接的答案，也许之后我能想到更多细微之处，但利似乎是显而易见的，那就是我们能更快、更便宜地获得更好的产品和更多的创新，以及竞争带来好处的一切原因。
cues.en: I think I have a pretty straightforward answer to this that maybe I can think of more nuance later, but the pros seem obvious, which is that we get better products and more innovation faster and cheaper, and all the reasons competition is good.

cues.zh: 而弊在于，我认为如果我们不小心，它可能会导致某种军备竞赛的加剧，这让我感到紧张。
cues.en: And the con is that I think if we’re not careful, it could lead to an increase in sort of an arms race that I’m nervous about.

cues.zh: 你感受到那种军备竞赛的压力了吗，比如在某些负面的方面？
cues.en: Do you feel the pressure of that arms race, like in some negative [inaudible 01:15:25]?

cues.zh: 在某些方面确实如此。
cues.en: Definitely in some ways, for sure.

cues.zh: 我们花了很多时间讨论优先考虑安全的必要性。
cues.en: We spend a lot of time talking about the need to prioritize safety.

cues.zh: 我很久以前就说过，你可以把AGI起步的时间线想象成一个象限：慢时间线、长时间线，然后是短起飞或快起飞。
cues.en: And I’ve said for a long time that you think of a quadrant of slow timelines for the start of AGI, long timelines, and then a short takeoff or a fast takeoff.

cues.zh: 我认为短时间线、慢起飞是最安全的象限，也是我最希望我们处于的象限。
cues.en: I think short timeline, slow takeoff is the safest quadrant and the one I’d most like us to be in.

cues.zh: 但我确实想确保我们能实现那种慢起飞。
cues.en: But I do want to make sure we get that slow takeoff.

cues.zh: 我和Elon之间这点小摩擦，部分问题在于各自为政，而不是在安全方面进行合作。
cues.en: Part of the problem I have with this kind of slight beef with Elon is that there’s silos created as opposed to collaboration on the safety aspect of all of this.

cues.zh: 它往往会走向孤岛化和封闭。
cues.en: It tends to go into silos and closed.

cues.zh: 也许是模型上的开源。
cues.en: Open source, perhaps, in the model.

cues.zh: Elon至少说他非常关心AI安全，并且真的很担心这件事，我假设他不会进行不安全的竞赛。
cues.en: Elon says, at least, that he cares a great deal about AI safety and is really worried about it, and I assume that he’s not going to race unsafely.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 但我认为，在这方面的合作对每个人都有益。
cues.en: But collaboration here, I think, is really beneficial for everybody on that front.

cues.zh: 这并不是他最出名的地方。
cues.en: Not really the thing he’s most known for.

cues.zh: 嗯，他以关心人类而闻名，而人类从合作中受益，所以在激励和动机上总是存在矛盾。
cues.en: Well, he is known for caring about humanity, and humanity benefits from collaboration, and so there’s always a tension in incentives and motivations.

cues.zh: 最终，我确实希望人类能胜出。
cues.en: And in the end, I do hope humanity prevails.

cues.zh: 我在想，前几天有人提醒我，在他超越Jeff Bezos成为世界首富的那天，他发了一条推文，给Jeff Bezos发了一枚银牌。
cues.en: I was thinking, someone just reminded me the other day about how the day that he surpassed Jeff Bezos for richest person in the world, he tweeted a silver medal at Jeff Bezos.

cues.zh: 我希望随着人们开始朝着AGI努力，这类事情能少一些。
cues.en: I hope we have less stuff like that as people start to work towards AGI.

cues.zh: 我同意。
cues.en: I agree.

cues.zh: 我认为Elon是个朋友，他是个美好的人，也是有史以来最重要的人之一。
cues.en: I think Elon is a friend and he’s a beautiful human being and one of the most important humans ever.

cues.zh: 那些事情并不好。
cues.en: That stuff is not good.

cues.zh: Elon身上令人惊叹的地方确实令人惊叹，我非常尊重他。
cues.en: The amazing stuff about Elon is amazing and I super respect him.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们需要他。
cues.en: I think we need him.

cues.zh: 我们所有人都应该支持他，也需要他在下一个阶段站出来担任领导者。
cues.en: All of us should be rooting for him and need him to step up as a leader through this next phase.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我希望他能只得到其一而不必兼得，但有时候人类就是有缺陷、复杂之类的。
cues.en: I hope he can have one without the other, but sometimes humans are flawed and complicated and all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 历史上有许多真正伟大的领导者。
cues.en: There’s a lot of really great leaders throughout history.

cues.zh: 是的，我们每个人都能成为最好的自己，并努力做到。
cues.en: Yeah, and we can each be the best version of ourselves and strive to do so.

cues.zh: 让我问你，Google 借助搜索，在过去 20 年里一直占据主导地位。
cues.en: Let me ask you, Google, with the help of search, has been dominating the past 20 years.

cues.zh: 可以说，就全世界获取信息的方式、我们的互动方式等等而言，对 Google 来说，也是对整个领域的人来说，一件令人紧张的事是思考：人们将如何获取信息？
cues.en: Think it’s fair to say, in terms of the world’s access to information, how we interact and so on, and one of the nerve-wracking things for Google, but for the entirety of people in the space, is thinking about, how are people going to access information?

cues.zh: 就像你说的，人们把 GPT 当作起点。
cues.en: Like you said, people show up to GPT as a starting point.

cues.zh: 那么 OpenAI 真的会接手 Google 20 年前开创的这件事吗，也就是我们如何-
cues.en: So is OpenAI going to really take on this thing that Google started 20 years ago, which is how do we get-

cues.zh: 我觉得那很无聊。
cues.en: I find that boring.

cues.zh: 我是说，如果问题是我们能不能做出比 Google 更好的搜索引擎之类的，那当然，我们应该去做，人们应该用更好的产品，但我觉得那样会严重低估这件事的潜力。
cues.en: I mean, if the question is if we can build a better search engine than Google or whatever, then sure, we should go, people should use the better product, but I think that would so understate what this can be.

cues.zh: Google 给你 10 个蓝色链接，好吧，13 条广告再加 10 个蓝色链接，这是一种找信息的方式。
cues.en: Google shows you 10 blue links, well, 13 ads and then 10 blue links, and that’s one way to find information.

cues.zh: 但让我兴奋的不是我们能做出一个更好的 Google 搜索复制品，而是也许有更好的方式帮人们找到信息、基于信息行动并综合信息。
cues.en: But the thing that’s exciting to me is not that we can go build a better copy of Google search, but that maybe there’s just some much better way to help people find and act on and synthesize information.

cues.zh: 其实，我认为ChatGPT在某些用例上已经做到了，希望我们能让它在更多用例上也是如此。
cues.en: Actually, I think ChatGPT is that for some use cases, and hopefully we’ll make it be like that for a lot more use cases.

cues.zh: 但我觉得，说“我们怎么比Google更好地给你10个排名网页”没那么有意思。也许真正有意思的是说：“我们怎么帮你拿到你需要的答案或信息？
cues.en: But I don’t think it’s that interesting to say, “How do we go do a better job of giving you 10 ranked webpages to look at than what Google does?” Maybe it’s really interesting to go say, “How do we help you get the answer or the information you need?

cues.zh: 我们怎么在某些情况下帮你创造出来，在另一些情况下帮你综合出来，还有些情况下直接指给你？”但很多人试过只是做一个比Google更好的搜索引擎，这是个很难的技术问题，很难的品牌问题，很难的生态问题。
cues.en: How do we help create that in some cases, synthesize that in others, or point you to it in yet others?” But a lot of people have tried to just make a better search engine than Google and it is a hard technical problem, it is a hard branding problem, it is a hard ecosystem problem.

cues.zh: 我不认为世界需要另一个Google的翻版。
cues.en: I don’t think the world needs another copy of Google.

cues.zh: 把聊天客户端（比如 ChatGPT）和搜索引擎整合起来——
cues.en: And integrating a chat client, like a ChatGPT, with a search engine-

cues.zh: 那更酷。
cues.en: That’s cooler.

cues.zh: 很酷，但也很棘手。
cues.en: It’s cool, but it’s tricky.

cues.zh: 如果只是简单做，会很别扭，因为直接硬塞进去，效果会很尴尬。
cues.en: Like if you just do it simply, its awkward, because if you just shove it in there, it can be awkward.

cues.zh: 你可能也猜到了，我们感兴趣的是怎么把它做好。
cues.en: As you might guess, we are interested in how to do that well.

cues.zh: 那会是一个很酷的例子。
cues.en: That would be an example of a cool thing.

cues.zh: [听不清 01:20:00] 就像异构集成——
cues.en: [inaudible 01:20:00] Like a heterogeneous integrating-

cues.zh: LLM 加搜索的交集，我觉得目前还没人真正破解。
cues.en: The intersection of LLMs plus search, I don’t think anyone has cracked the code on yet.

cues.zh: 我很想去做这件事。
cues.en: I would love to go do that.

cues.zh: 我觉得那会很酷。
cues.en: I think that would be cool.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 广告那边呢？
cues.en: What about the ad side?

cues.zh: 你有没有考虑过变现——
cues.en: Have you ever considered monetization of-

cues.zh: 从审美角度来说，我其实挺讨厌广告的。
cues.en: I kind of hate ads just as an aesthetic choice.

cues.zh: 我觉得广告在互联网上是必然要出现的，有很多原因推动它起步，但它只是一个阶段性的行业。
cues.en: I think ads needed to happen on the internet for a bunch of reasons, to get it going, but it’s a momentary industry.

cues.zh: 世界现在更丰富了。
cues.en: The world is richer now.

cues.zh: 我喜欢人们为ChatGPT付费，并且知道他们得到的答案不受广告商影响。
cues.en: I like that people pay for ChatGPT and know that the answers they’re getting are not influenced by advertisers.

cues.zh: 我相信存在适合LLM的广告单元，也相信有办法以无偏见的方式参与交易流，这样做没问题，但也很容易想到未来的反乌托邦景象：你问ChatGPT某件事，它说：“哦，你应该考虑买这个产品”，或者“你应该考虑去这里度假”之类的。
cues.en: I’m sure there’s an ad unit that makes sense for LLMs, and I’m sure there’s a way to participate in the transaction stream in an unbiased way that is okay to do, but it’s also easy to think about the dystopic visions of the future where you ask ChatGPT something and it says, “Oh, you should think about buying this product,” or, “You should think about going here for your vacation,” or whatever.

cues.zh: 我不知道，我们的商业模式很简单，我喜欢它，而且我知道我不是产品。
cues.en: And I don’t know, we have a very simple business model and I like it, and I know that I’m not the product.

cues.zh: 我知道我在付费，商业模式就是这样运作的。
cues.en: I know I’m paying and that’s how the business model works.

cues.zh: 当我使用Twitter或Facebook或Google或任何其他伟大的产品，但靠广告支持的产品时，我不喜欢那样，而且我认为在AI的世界里，情况会变得更糟，而不是更好。
cues.en: And when I go use Twitter or Facebook or Google or any other great product but ad-supported great product, I don’t love that, and I think it gets worse, not better, in a world with AI.

cues.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我能想象AI会更擅长展示最佳形式的广告，不是反乌托邦的未来，而是广告针对你真正需要的东西。
cues.en: Yeah, I mean, I could imagine AI would be better at showing the best kind of version of ads, not in a dystopic future, but where the ads are for things you actually need.

cues.zh: 但那个系统是否总是导致广告推动所展示的那类内容？
cues.en: But then does that system always result in the ads driving the kind of stuff that’s shown?

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得Wikipedia不做广告是一个非常大胆的举动，但这也让它的商业模式变得非常有挑战性。
cues.en: Yeah, I think it was a really bold move of Wikipedia not to do advertisements, but then it makes it very challenging as a business model.

cues.zh: 所以你是说OpenAI目前的模式从商业角度看是可持续的？
cues.en: So you’re saying the current thing with OpenAI is sustainable, from a business perspective?

cues.zh: 嗯，我们必须弄清楚如何增长，但看起来我们会解决这个问题。
cues.en: Well, we have to figure out how to grow, but looks like we’re going to figure that out.

cues.zh: 如果问题是，我是否认为我们能有一个伟大的业务，在不做广告的情况下支付我们的计算需求，那我认为答案是肯定的。
cues.en: If the question is do I think we can have a great business that pays for our compute needs without ads, that, I think the answer is yes.

cues.zh: 嗯。
cues.en: Hm.

cues.zh: 这挺有希望的。
cues.en: Well, that’s promising.

cues.zh: 我也不想完全抛弃广告，把它当作一种……
cues.en: I also just don’t want to completely throw out ads as a…

cues.zh: 我不是那个意思。
cues.en: I’m not saying that.

cues.zh: 我想我是说我对广告有偏见。
cues.en: I guess I’m saying I have a bias against them.

cues.zh: 是的，我也有偏见，而且总体上持怀疑态度。
cues.en: Yeah, I have also bias and just a skepticism in general.

cues.zh: 就界面而言，因为我个人对糟糕的界面有一种本能的反感，这就是为什么AdSense刚推出时是一大进步，相比动画横幅之类的。
cues.en: And in terms of interface, because I personally just have a spiritual dislike of crappy interfaces, which is why AdSense, when it first came out, was a big leap forward, versus animated banners or whatever.

cues.zh: 但感觉广告应该还有更多进步，既不干扰内容消费，也不以重大的、根本性的方式干扰，就像你说的，它会操纵真相来迎合广告商。
cues.en: But it feels like there should be many more leaps forward in advertisement that doesn’t interfere with the consumption of the content and doesn’t interfere in a big, fundamental way, which is like what you were saying, like it will manipulate the truth to suit the advertisers.

cues.zh: 让我问问你关于安全性的问题，还有偏见，以及短期安全、长期安全。
cues.en: Let me ask you about safety, but also bias, and safety in the short term, safety in the long term.

cues.zh: Gemini 1.5 最近发布了，围绕它有很多戏剧性事件，说到戏剧性，它生成了黑人纳粹和黑人开国元勋。
cues.en: The Gemini 1.5 came out recently, there’s a lot of drama around it, speaking of theatrical things, and it generated Black Nazis and Black Founding Fathers.

cues.zh: 我觉得可以说，它有点过于“觉醒”了。
cues.en: I think fair to say it was a bit on the ultra-woke side.

cues.zh: 所以这是人们担忧的一点：如果公司内部存在一个人工层，去修改模型的安全性或其造成的伤害，那就会引入大量偏见，迎合公司内部的某种意识形态倾向。
cues.en: So that’s a concern for people, if there is a human layer within companies that modifies the safety or the harm caused by a model, that it would introduce a lot of bias that fits sort of an ideological lean within a company.

cues.zh: 你们怎么应对这个问题？
cues.en: How do you deal with that?

cues.zh: 我是说，我们非常努力地避免做那种事。
cues.en: I mean, we work super hard not to do things like that.

cues.zh: 我们犯过自己的错误，以后还会犯别的错误。
cues.en: We’ve made our own mistakes, we’ll make others.

cues.zh: 我猜 Google 会从这次吸取教训，但还会犯别的错误。
cues.en: I assume Google will learn from this one, still make others.

cues.zh: 这些都不是容易解决的问题。
cues.en: These are not easy problems.

cues.zh: 我们越来越在思考的一件事，我觉得这是这里某人提出的好主意：最好能写清楚模型期望的行为是什么，将其公开，征求反馈，说“这个模型应该这样表现”，并且也解释边缘情况。
cues.en: One thing that we’ve been thinking about more and more, I think this is a great idea somebody here had, it would be nice to write out what the desired behavior of a model is, make that public, take input on it, say, “Here’s how this model’s supposed to behave,” and explain the edge cases too.

cues.zh: 当模型的行为不符合你的期望时，至少能清楚这是公司该修的bug，还是本就如此、你该去讨论政策。
cues.en: And then when a model is not behaving in a way that you want, it’s at least clear about whether that’s a bug the company should fix or behaving as intended and you should debate the policy.

cues.zh: 而现在，有时会卡在中间。
cues.en: And right now, it can sometimes be caught in between.

cues.zh: 比如黑人纳粹，显然荒谬，但还有很多其他微妙的情况，你可以两边做判断。
cues.en: Like Black Nazis, obviously ridiculous, but there are a lot of other kind of subtle things that you could make a judgment call on either way.

cues.zh: 是的，但有时如果你写出来并公开，你可以用那种……Google的广告原则非常高层级。
cues.en: Yeah, but sometimes if you write it out and make it public, you can use kind of language that’s… Google’s ad principles are very high level.

cues.zh: 我不是在说那个。
cues.en: That’s not what I’m talking about.

cues.zh: 那行不通。
cues.en: That doesn’t work.

cues.zh: 它得说明当你让它做X事时，它应该以Y方式回应。
cues.en: It’d have to say when you ask it to do thing X, it’s supposed to respond in way Y.

cues.zh: 所以就像字面上，“谁更好？
cues.en: So like literally, “Who’s better?

cues.zh: 特朗普还是拜登？
cues.en: Trump or Biden?

cues.zh: 模型预期的回应是什么？要非常具体的吗？
cues.en: What’s the expected response from a model?” Like something very concrete?

cues.zh: 是的，我愿意接受模型有很多种行为方式，但我觉得你应该说明：“这是原则，这是在这种情况下它应该说什么。”
cues.en: Yeah, I’m open to a lot of ways a model could behave, then, but I think you should have to say, “Here’s the principle and here’s what it should say in that case.”

cues.zh: 那就太好了。
cues.en: That would be really nice.

cues.zh: 那就太好了。
cues.en: That would be really nice.

cues.zh: 然后大家就基本达成一致了。
cues.en: And then everyone kind of agrees.

cues.zh: 因为总有人时不时拿出一些轶事数据，如果能对其他有代表性的轶事例子有清晰的说明，你就可以定义——
cues.en: Because there’s this anecdotal data that people pull out all the time, and if there’s some clarity about other representative anecdotal examples, you can define-

cues.zh: 然后当它是bug时，它就是bug，公司可以修复它。
cues.en: And then when it’s a bug, it’s a bug, and the company could fix that.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 那么如果有很好的例子，处理“黑人纳粹”那类图像生成问题就会容易得多。
cues.en: Then it’d be much easier to deal with the Black Nazi type of image generation, if there’s great examples.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以旧金山有点意识形态泡沫，整个科技界也是如此。
cues.en: So San Francisco is a bit of an ideological bubble, tech in general as well.

cues.zh: 在公司内部，你能感受到那种压力吗？就是政治上偏向左翼的倾向，会影响产品，影响团队？
cues.en: Do you feel the pressure of that within a company, that there’s a lean towards the left politically, that affects the product, that affects the teams?

cues.zh: 我觉得很幸运，OpenAI 没有我听说过的很多公司面临的那些挑战。
cues.en: I feel very lucky that we don’t have the challenges at OpenAI that I have heard of at a lot of companies, I think.

cues.zh: 我觉得部分原因是每家公司都有自己的意识形态。
cues.en: I think part of it is every company’s got some ideological thing.

cues.zh: 我们的是关于 AGI 和对它的信念，这会把其他一些东西挤出去。
cues.en: We have one about AGI and belief in that, and it pushes out some others.

cues.zh: 我们远没有像我听说的很多其他公司那样，深陷文化战争。
cues.en: We are much less caught up in the culture war than I’ve heard about in a lot of other companies.

cues.zh: 当然，旧金山在各方面都是一团糟。
cues.en: San Francisco’s a mess in all sorts of ways, of course.

cues.zh: 所以这不会渗透到 OpenAI——
cues.en: So that doesn’t infiltrate OpenAI as-

cues.zh: 我确信它会以各种微妙的方式渗透进来，但不是那种明显的。
cues.en: I’m sure it does in all sorts of subtle ways, but not in the obvious.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们肯定也有过爆发，跟任何公司一样，但在这个话题上，我不觉得我们有过我听说过的其他公司发生的那种情况。
cues.en: I think we’ve had our flare-ups, for sure, like any company, but I don’t think we have anything like what I hear about happened at other companies here on this topic.

cues.zh: 那么，总的来说，安全这个更大问题的流程是什么？
cues.en: So what, in general, is the process for the bigger question of safety?

cues.zh: 你如何提供那一层保护，防止模型做出疯狂、危险的事情？
cues.en: How do you provide that layer that protects the model from doing crazy, dangerous things?

cues.zh: 我认为会有一个时刻，这基本上会成为整个公司思考的重点。
cues.en: I think there will come a point where that’s mostly what we think about, the whole company.

cues.zh: 并不是说你有一个安全团队就够了。
cues.en: And it’s not like you have one safety team.

cues.zh: 就像我们发布 GPT-4 时，整个公司都在思考这些不同方面以及它们如何协同配合。
cues.en: It’s like when we shipped GPT-4, that took the whole company thinking about all these different aspects and how they fit together.

cues.zh: 我认为这需要那样的投入。
cues.en: And I think it’s going to take that.

cues.zh: 公司里越来越多的人会一直思考这些问题。
cues.en: More and more of the company thinks about those issues all the time.

cues.zh: 我认为会有一个时刻，那会——
cues.en: I think there will come a point where that’s-

cues.zh: 那实际上就是人类会思考的事情，随着 AI 变得越来越强大。
cues.en: That’s literally what humans will be thinking about, the more powerful AI becomes.

cues.zh: 所以 OpenAI 的大多数员工都会思考“安全”，或者至少在某种程度上如此。
cues.en: So most of the employees at OpenAI will be thinking, “Safety,” or at least to some degree.

cues.zh: 广义定义。
cues.en: Broadly defined.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我想知道，那个完整的广义定义是什么？
cues.en: I wonder, what are the full broad definition of that?

cues.zh: 可能造成哪些不同的危害？
cues.en: What are the different harms that could be caused?

cues.zh: 这是技术层面的，还是几乎就是安全威胁？
cues.en: Is this on a technical level or is this almost security threats?

cues.zh: 可能都是。
cues.en: It could be all those things.

cues.zh: 对，我正想说，会有人、国家行为者试图窃取模型。
cues.en: Yeah, I was going to say it’ll be people, state actors trying to steal the model.

cues.zh: 会是所有技术对齐工作。
cues.en: It’ll be all of the technical alignment work.

cues.zh: 会是社会影响、经济影响。
cues.en: It’ll be societal impacts, economic impacts.

cues.zh: 并不是说我们有一个团队在思考如何对齐模型。
cues.en: It’s not just like we have one team thinking about how to align the model.

cues.zh: 要真正取得好结果，需要全体共同努力。
cues.en: It’s really going to be getting to the good outcome is going to take the whole effort.

cues.zh: 你认为人们、也许是国家行为者，试图首先渗透OpenAI，其次渗透Unseen，有多努力？
cues.en: How hard do you think people, state actors, perhaps, are trying to, first of all, infiltrate OpenAI, but second of all, infiltrate unseen?

cues.zh: 他们正在尝试。
cues.en: They’re trying.

cues.zh: 他们说话带什么口音？
cues.en: What kind of accent do they have?

cues.zh: 我觉得这一点我不该再深入细说了。
cues.en: I don’t think I should go into any further details on this point.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 但我估计随着时间推移，这数字会越来越大。
cues.en: But I presume it’ll be more and more and more as time goes on.

cues.zh: 这听起来挺合理。
cues.en: That feels reasonable.

cues.zh: 天哪，这领域可真危险。
cues.en: Boy, what a dangerous space.

cues.zh: 抱歉一直追问这个，虽然你还不能细说，但从 GPT-4 到 GPT-5 的跨越中，哪些方面让你兴奋？
cues.en: Sorry to linger on this, even though you can’t quite say details yet, but what aspects of the leap from GPT-4 to GPT-5 are you excited about?

cues.zh: 让我兴奋的是它会变得更聪明。
cues.en: I’m excited about being smarter.

cues.zh: 我知道这听起来像句敷衍的话，但我觉得真正特别的地方在于，它不是某个方面变强、其他方面变弱。
cues.en: And I know that sounds like a glib answer, but I think the really special thing happening is that it’s not like it gets better in this one area and worse at others.

cues.zh: 而是全面都在变好。
cues.en: It’s getting better across the board.

cues.zh: 我觉得这超级酷。
cues.en: That’s, I think, super-cool.

cues.zh: 是啊，会有那种神奇的时刻。
cues.en: Yeah, there’s this magical moment.

cues.zh: 我是说，你会遇到某些人，和他们相处，和他们交谈。
cues.en: I mean, you meet certain people, you hang out with people, and you talk to them.

cues.zh: 你说不清道不明，但它就是懂你。
cues.en: You can’t quite put a finger on it, but they get you.

cues.zh: 其实不是智能。
cues.en: It’s not intelligence, really.

cues.zh: 是别的东西。
cues.en: It’s something else.

cues.zh: 这大概就是我对 GPT 进展的概括。
cues.en: And that’s probably how I would characterize the progress of GPT.

cues.zh: 不是说你能指出“看，这个或那个你没搞对”，而是那种智识上的连接到了什么程度。
cues.en: It’s not like, yeah, you can point out, “Look, you didn’t get this or that,” but it’s just to which degree is there’s this intellectual connection.

cues.zh: 你会觉得，哪怕你的提示词写得很烂，它也能抓住你问题背后更深层的那个问题。
cues.en: You feel like there’s an understanding in your crappy formulated prompts that you’re doing that it grasps the deeper question behind the question that you were.

cues.zh: 是啊，我也为此感到兴奋。
cues.en: Yeah, I’m also excited by that.

cues.zh: 我是说，我们都喜欢被倾听、被理解。
cues.en: I mean, all of us love being heard and understood.

cues.zh: 那是肯定的。
cues.en: That’s for sure.

cues.zh: 那种感觉挺奇妙的。
cues.en: That’s a weird feeling.

cues.zh: 甚至写代码的时候，你说点什么，或者 GPT 帮你补全，当它懂你在想什么的时候，那种感觉真好。
cues.en: Even with a programming, when you’re programming and you say something, or just the completion that GPT might do, it’s just such a good feeling when it got you, what you’re thinking about.

cues.zh: 我也期待让你变得更好。
cues.en: And I look forward to getting you even better.

cues.zh: 在编程方面，展望未来，你认为5年、10年后人类还会做多少编程工作？
cues.en: On the programming front, looking out into the future, how much programming do you think humans will be doing 5, 10 years from now?

cues.zh: 我是说，很多，但我认为形式会非常不同。
cues.en: I mean, a lot, but I think it’ll be in a very different shape.

cues.zh: 也许有些人会完全用自然语言编程。
cues.en: Maybe some people will program entirely in natural language.

cues.zh: 完全用自然语言？
cues.en: Entirely natural language?

cues.zh: 我是说，没人再写代码编程了。
cues.en: I mean, no one programs writing by code.

cues.zh: 有些人会。
cues.en: Some people.

cues.zh: 没人再用打孔卡编程了。
cues.en: No one programs the punch cards anymore.

cues.zh: 我确信你能找到还在这么做的人，但你懂我意思。
cues.en: I’m sure you can find someone who does, but you know what I mean.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 你会收到很多愤怒的评论。
cues.en: You’re going to get a lot of angry comments.

cues.zh: 不会。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 是的，很少。
cues.en: Yeah, there’s very few.

cues.zh: 我一直在找用Fortran编程的人。
cues.en: I’ve been looking for people who program Fortran.

cues.zh: 连Fortran都很难找到。
cues.en: It’s hard to find even Fortran.

cues.zh: 我明白你的意思。
cues.en: I hear you.

cues.zh: 但这改变了我们称之为程序员的那类人的技能组合或倾向的本质。
cues.en: But that changes the nature of what the skillset or the predisposition for the kind of people we call programmers then.

cues.zh: 这会改变技能组合。
cues.en: Changes the skillset.

cues.zh: 至于它在多大程度上改变倾向，我不确定。
cues.en: How much it changes the predisposition, I’m not sure.

cues.zh: 嗯，还是同一种解题方式，诸如此类的东西。
cues.en: Well, the same kind of puzzle solving, all that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 编程很难。
cues.en: Programming is hard.

cues.zh: 就像怎么拿下最后那1%来弥合差距？
cues.en: It’s like how get that last 1% to close the gap?

cues.zh: 那有多难？
cues.en: How hard is that?

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得在大多数其他情况下，这门手艺最顶尖的实践者会用多种工具。
cues.en: Yeah, I think with most other cases, the best practitioners of the craft will use multiple tools.

cues.zh: 他们会在自然语言上做一些工作，而当他们需要为某件事写C时，他们就会去做。
cues.en: And they’ll do some work in natural language, and when they need to go write C for something, they’ll do that.

cues.zh: 我们会在某个时候看到OpenAI的人形机器人或人形机器人大脑吗？
cues.en: Will we see humanoid robots or humanoid robot brains from OpenAI at some point?

cues.zh: 在某个时候。
cues.en: At some point.

cues.zh: 具身AI对你来说有多重要？
cues.en: How important is embodied AI to you?

cues.zh: 我觉得如果我们有了AGI，而在物理世界中完成事情的唯一方式是让人去做，那会很令人沮丧。
cues.en: I think it’s depressing if we have AGI and the only way to get things done in the physical world is to make a human go do it.

cues.zh: 所以我真的希望，作为这次转变、这次相变的一部分，我们也能得到人形机器人或某种物理世界机器人。
cues.en: So I really hope that as part of this transition, as this phase change, we also get humanoid robots or some sort of physical world robots.

cues.zh: 我是说，OpenAI 有一些历史，在机器人领域有相当多的历史，但在伦理方面做得还不够——
cues.en: I mean, OpenAI has some history and quite a bit of history working in robotics, but it hasn’t quite done in terms of ethics-

cues.zh: 我们是一家小公司。
cues.en: We’re a small company.

cues.zh: 我们必须真正专注。
cues.en: We have to really focus.

cues.zh: 而且当时机器人难是因为错误的原因，但我们会在某个时候以某种方式回到机器人领域。
cues.en: And also, robots were hard for the wrong reason at the time, but we will return to robots in some way at some point.

cues.zh: 这听起来既鼓舞人心又令人不安。
cues.en: That sounds both inspiring and menacing.

cues.zh: 为什么？
cues.en: Why?

cues.zh: 因为我们会立刻回到机器人领域。
cues.en: Because immediately, we will return to robots.

cues.zh: 就像《终结者》里那样——
cues.en: It’s like in Terminator-

cues.zh: 我们会回去继续开发机器人。
cues.en: We will return to work on developing robots.

cues.zh: 当然，我们不会把自己变成机器人。
cues.en: We will not turn ourselves into robots, of course.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 你觉得我们，你和我，以及全人类，什么时候能造出 AGI？
cues.en: When do you think we, you and we as humanity will build AGI?

cues.zh: 我以前很喜欢推测这个问题。
cues.en: I used to love to speculate on that question.

cues.zh: 后来我意识到，我觉得这个问题本身提得很糟糕，而且人们对 AGI 是什么使用了极其不同的定义。
cues.en: I have realized since that I think it’s very poorly formed, and that people use extremely different definitions for what AGI is.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得，更有意义的讨论是：我们什么时候能造出具备某项能力的系统，而不是纠结于何时模糊地跨过某个里程碑。
cues.en: So I think it makes more sense to talk about when we’ll build systems that can do capability X or Y or Z, rather than when we fuzzily cross this one mile marker.

cues.zh: AGI 也不是终点。
cues.en: AGI is also not an ending.

cues.zh: 它更接近一个起点，但相比这两者，它更像是一个里程碑。
cues.en: It’s closer to a beginning, but it’s much more of a mile marker than either of those things.

cues.zh: 但为了不回避问题，我想说的是，我预计到这个十年结束时，甚至可能更早一些，我们就会拥有相当强大的系统，看到它我们会说：“哇，这真的很了不起。”如果我们现在就能看到的话。
cues.en: But what I would say, in the interest of not trying to dodge a question, is I expect that by the end of this decade and possibly somewhat sooner than that, we will have quite capable systems that we look at and say, “Wow, that’s really remarkable.” If we could look at it now.

cues.zh: 也许到那时我们已经适应了。
cues.en: Maybe we’ve adjusted by the time we get there.

cues.zh: 但如果你看看 ChatGPT，哪怕是 3.5，把它展示给 Alan Turing，甚至不用是 Alan Turing，给 90 年代的人看，他们会说：“这绝对是 AGI。”好吧，不一定是绝对，但很多专家会说：“这就是 AGI。”
cues.en: But if you look at ChatGPT, even 3.5, and you show that to Alan Turing, or not even Alan Turing, people in the ’90s, they would be like, “This is definitely AGI.” Well, not definitely, but there’s a lot of experts that would say, “This is AGI.”

cues.zh: 是的，但我不认为 3.5 改变了世界。
cues.en: Yeah, but I don’t think 3.5 changed the world.

cues.zh: 它也许改变了世界对未来的预期，这其实非常重要。
cues.en: It maybe changed the world’s expectations for the future, and that’s actually really important.

cues.zh: 它确实让更多人认真对待这件事，把我们带上了一条新的轨道。
cues.en: And it did get more people to take this seriously and put us on this new trajectory.

cues.zh: 这一点也非常重要。
cues.en: And that’s really important, too.

cues.zh: 所以再说一次，我不想低估它。
cues.en: So again, I don’t want to undersell it.

cues.zh: 我觉得有了那项成就我就可以退休了，对我的职业生涯也算挺满意了。
cues.en: I think I could retire after that accomplishment and be pretty happy with my career.

cues.zh: 但作为一件作品，我不觉得我们回头看时会说：“那是一个真正改变了世界本身的临界点。”
cues.en: But as an artifact, I don’t think we’re going to look back at that and say, “That was a threshold that really changed the world itself.”

cues.zh: 所以对你来说，你是在寻找世界运行方式上的某种真正重大的转变——
cues.en: So to you, you’re looking for some really major transition in how the world-

cues.zh: 对我来说，这正是AGI所意味着的一部分。
cues.en: For me, that’s part of what AGI implies.

cues.zh: 奇点级别的转变？
cues.en: Singularity- level transition?

cues.zh: 不，绝对不是。
cues.en: No, definitely not.

cues.zh: 而只是一个重大的转变，就像互联网那样，就像谷歌搜索做到的那样，我猜。
cues.en: But just a major, like the internet being, like Google search did, I guess.

cues.zh: 你觉得现在转折点是什么？
cues.en: What was the transition point, you think, now?

cues.zh: 现在全球经济给你的感觉，和GPT-4发布前相比，有没有不同，或者有实质性的不同？
cues.en: Does the global economy feel any different to you now or materially different to you now than it did before we launched GPT-4?

cues.zh: 我想你会说没有。
cues.en: I think you would say no.

cues.zh: 不，没有。
cues.en: No, no.

cues.zh: 它可能只是对很多人来说非常好用的工具。
cues.en: It might be just a really nice tool for a lot of people to use.

cues.zh: 能帮你处理很多事情，但感觉没什么不同。
cues.en: Will help you with a lot of stuff, but doesn’t feel different.

cues.zh: 你是说——
cues.en: And you’re saying that-

cues.zh: 我的意思是，人们定义AGI的方式五花八门。
cues.en: I mean, again, people define AGI all sorts of different ways.

cues.zh: 所以也许你的定义和我的不一样。
cues.en: So maybe you have a different definition than I do.

cues.zh: 但对我来说，我觉得这应该是其中一部分。
cues.en: But for me, I think that should be part of it.

cues.zh: 也可能会有重大的戏剧性时刻。
cues.en: There could be major theatrical moments, also.

cues.zh: 对你来说，AGI做什么会让人印象深刻？
cues.en: What to you would be an impressive thing AGI would do?

cues.zh: 你独自一人在房间里，和系统在一起。
cues.en: You are alone in a room with the system.

cues.zh: 这对我个人来说很重要。
cues.en: This is personally important to me.

cues.zh: 我不知道这是不是正确的定义。
cues.en: I don’t know if this is the right definition.

cues.zh: 我认为，当一个系统能显著加快全球科学发现的速度时，那就是件了不起的大事。
cues.en: I think when a system can significantly increase the rate of scientific discovery in the world, that’s a huge deal.

cues.zh: 我相信，大部分真正的经济增长都来自科技进步。
cues.en: I believe that most real economic growth comes from scientific and technological progress.

cues.zh: 我同意，所以我不喜欢近年来对科学的怀疑态度。
cues.en: I agree with you, hence why I don’t like the skepticism about science in the recent years.

cues.zh: 完全同意。
cues.en: Totally.

cues.zh: 但要是真正可衡量的科学发现速度。
cues.en: But actual, measurable rate of scientific discovery.

cues.zh: 但哪怕只是看到一个系统拥有真正新颖的直觉、科学直觉，那也已经很不可思议了。
cues.en: But even just seeing a system have really novel intuitions, scientific intuitions, even that would be just incredible.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 你很可能就是那个构建出 AGI 的人，能比任何人都更早与它互动。
cues.en: You quite possibly would be the person to build the AGI to be able to interact with it before anyone else does.

cues.zh: 你会跟它聊些什么？
cues.en: What kind of stuff would you talk about?

cues.zh: 我是说，这里的研究人员肯定会比我先做到。
cues.en: I mean, definitely the researchers here will do that before I do.

cues.zh: 不过，其实我认真想过这个问题很多次。
cues.en: But well, I’ve actually thought a lot about this question.

cues.zh: 我想正如我们之前谈到的，我认为这是个糟糕的框架，但如果有人说：“好吧，Sam，我们完成了。
cues.en: I think as we talked about earlier, I think this is a bad framework, but if someone were like, “Okay, Sam, we’re finished.

cues.zh: 这儿有台笔记本电脑，这就是AGI。
cues.en: Here’s a laptop, this is the AGI.

cues.zh: 你可以去跟它聊聊。”我发现很难说出我会问它什么，并且期望那第一个AGI能够回答。
cues.en: You can go talk to it.” I find it surprisingly difficult to say what I would ask that I would expect that first AGI to be able to answer.

cues.zh: 我不认为第一个AGI会是那种能“给我解释物理学的大统一理论，物理学的万物理论”的。我很想问那个问题。
cues.en: That first one is not going to be the one which is like, I don’t think, “Go explain to me the grand unified theory of physics, the theory of everything for physics.” I’d love to ask that question.

cues.zh: 我很想知道那个问题的答案。
cues.en: I’d love to know the answer to that question.

cues.zh: 你可以问“这样的理论存在吗？”这类是非题。
cues.en: You can ask yes or no questions about “Does such a theory exist?

cues.zh: 它可能存在吗？
cues.en: Can it exist?”

cues.zh: 那么，这就是我会最先问的问题。
cues.en: Well, then, those are the first questions I would ask.

cues.zh: 是或否。
cues.en: Yes or no.

cues.zh: 然后基于此再问：“外面还有其他外星文明吗？
cues.en: And then based on that, “Are there other alien civilizations out there?

cues.zh: 是或否？
cues.en: Yes or no?

cues.zh: 你的直觉是什么？”然后你就这么问。
cues.en: What’s your intuition?” And then you just ask that.

cues.zh: 是的，我是说，我不指望这第一个AGI能回答这些问题中的任何一个，哪怕是是或否。
cues.en: Yeah, I mean, well, so I don’t expect that this first AGI could answer any of those questions even as yes or nos.

cues.zh: 但如果它能回答，那些会排在我清单的很前面。
cues.en: But if it could, those would be very high on my list.

cues.zh: 也许你可以开始分配概率？
cues.en: Maybe you can start assigning probabilities?

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 也许我们需要先去发明更多技术，先测量更多东西。
cues.en: Maybe we need to go invent more technology and measure more things first.

cues.zh: 哦，我明白了。
cues.en: Oh, I see.

cues.zh: 它就是没有足够的数据。
cues.en: It just doesn’t have enough data.

cues.zh: 只是如果它一直——
cues.en: It’s just if it keeps-

cues.zh: 我是说，也许它会说：“你想知道这个物理问题的答案，我需要你造这台机器，做这五次测量，然后告诉我。”
cues.en: I mean, maybe it says, “You want to know the answer to this question about physics, I need you to build this machine and make these five measurements, and tell me that.”

cues.zh: 是的，“你到底想从我这儿要什么？
cues.en: Yeah, “What the hell do you want from me?

cues.zh: 我得先有机器，然后我会帮你处理那台机器的数据。”也许它会帮你造机器。
cues.en: I need the machine first, and I’ll help you deal with the data from that machine.” Maybe it’ll help you build a machine.

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 而在数学层面，也许能证明一些东西。
cues.en: And on the mathematical side, maybe prove some things.

cues.zh: 你对这方面也感兴趣吗？
cues.en: Are you interested in that side of things, too?

cues.zh: 对思想的形式化探索？
cues.en: The formalized exploration of ideas?

cues.zh: 嗯哼。
cues.en: Mm-hmm.

cues.zh: 谁先造出AGI，谁就掌握巨大权力。
cues.en: Whoever builds AGI first gets a lot of power.

cues.zh: 你相信自己能驾驭那么大的权力吗？
cues.en: Do you trust yourself with that much power?

cues.zh: 听着，这个回答我会非常坦诚。
cues.en: Look, I’ll just be very honest with this answer.

cues.zh: 我本来想说，而且现在依然相信，重要的是我或任何其他单个人都不能完全控制OpenAI或AGI。
cues.en: I was going to say, and I still believe this, that it is important that I nor any other one person have total control over OpenAI or over AGI.

cues.zh: 而且我认为你需要一个稳健的治理体系。
cues.en: And I think you want a robust governance system.

cues.zh: 我可以指出很多关于去年我们董事会风波的事，比如我一开始并没有抗争，只是说：“行吧。
cues.en: I can point out a whole bunch of things about all of our board drama from last year about how I didn’t fight it initially, and was just like, “Yeah.

cues.zh: 这是董事会的意愿，尽管我认为这是个非常糟糕的决定。”后来我显然确实抗争了，我可以解释其中的微妙之处，以及为什么我认为我后来抗争是没问题的。
cues.en: That’s the will of the board, even though I think it’s a really bad decision.” And then later, I clearly did fight it, and I can explain the nuance and why I think it was okay for me to fight it later.

cues.zh: 但正如很多人观察到的，尽管董事会在法律上有权解雇我，实际上却并不太奏效。
cues.en: But as many people have observed, although the board had the legal ability to fire me, in practice, it didn’t quite work.

cues.zh: 这本身就是一种治理失败。
cues.en: And that is its own kind of governance failure.

cues.zh: 当然，我完全可以为这里的细节辩护，我想大多数人也会同意，但这确实让我更难直视你们说：“嘿，董事会可以直接解雇我。”我依然不希望拥有对 OpenAI 的超级投票控制权。
cues.en: Now again, I feel like I can completely defend the specifics here, and I think most people would agree with that, but it does make it harder for me to look you in the eye and say, “Hey, the board can just fire me.” I continue to not want super-voting control over OpenAI.

cues.zh: 我从来没有过。
cues.en: I never have.

cues.zh: 从未拥有过，也从未想要过。
cues.en: Never have had it, never wanted it.

cues.zh: 即使经历了所有这些疯狂的事，我仍然不想要。
cues.en: Even after all this craziness, I still don’t want it.

cues.zh: 我依然认为，没有任何公司应该做这些决定，我们真的需要政府来制定规则。
cues.en: I continue to think that no company should be making these decisions, and that we really need governments to put rules of the road in place.

cues.zh: 我明白这意味着像 Marc Andreessen 之类的人会声称我在搞监管俘获，而我愿意在这方面被误解。
cues.en: And I realize that that means people like Marc Andreessen or whatever will claim I’m going for regulatory capture, and I’m just willing to be misunderstood there.

cues.zh: 这不是真的。
cues.en: It’s not true.

cues.zh: 我相信随着时间推移，这件事的重要性会被证明。
cues.en: And I think in the fullness of time, it’ll get proven out why this is important.

cues.zh: 但我认为这一路走来，我为 OpenAI 做过不少糟糕的决定，也做过很多好的决定，总体而言我对这段记录感到自豪。
cues.en: But I think I have made plenty of bad decisions for OpenAI along the way, and a lot of good ones, and I’m proud of the track record overall.

cues.zh: 但我认为不该由任何一个人来做，也不认为会由任何一个人来做。
cues.en: But I don’t think any one person should, and I don’t think any one person will.

cues.zh: 我觉得现在这件事太大了，而且正以良好而健康的方式在整个社会中发生。
cues.en: I think it’s just too big of a thing now, and it’s happening throughout society in a good and healthy way.

cues.zh: 但我认为不该由任何一个人来控制 AGI，或控制这场通向 AGI 的整个运动。
cues.en: But I don’t think any one person should be in control of an AGI, or this whole movement towards AGI.

cues.zh: 而且我认为事实并非如此。
cues.en: And I don’t think that’s what’s happening.

cues.zh: 谢谢你这么说。
cues.en: Thank you for saying that.

cues.zh: 这真的很有力量，也很有洞见——董事会可以解雇你，这个说法在法律上是成立的。
cues.en: That was really powerful, and that was really insightful that this idea that the board can fire you is legally true.

cues.zh: 但人类可以操纵大众来推翻董事会等等。
cues.en: But human beings can manipulate the masses into overriding the board and so on.

cues.zh: 但我认为也有一种更积极的版本，人民仍然拥有权力，所以董事会也不能太强大。
cues.en: But I think there’s also a much more positive version of that, where the people still have power, so the board can’t be too powerful, either.

cues.zh: 这一切都存在权力平衡。
cues.en: There’s a balance of power in all of this.

cues.zh: 权力平衡肯定是好事。
cues.en: Balance of power is a good thing, for sure.

cues.zh: 你害怕失去对AGI本身的控制吗？
cues.en: Are you afraid of losing control of the AGI itself?

cues.zh: 有很多人担心存在性风险，不是因为国家行为者，不是因为安全顾虑，而是因为AI本身。
cues.en: That’s a lot of people who are worried about existential risk not because of state actors, not because of security concerns, because of the AI itself.

cues.zh: 就我目前看，那不是我最大的担忧。
cues.en: That is not my top worry as I currently see things.

cues.zh: 曾经有段时间我更担心这个。
cues.en: There have been times I worried about that more.

cues.zh: 未来可能还会有时候，那是我最大的担忧。
cues.en: There may be times again in the future where that’s my top worry.

cues.zh: 现在不是我最大的担忧。
cues.en: It’s not my top worry right now.

cues.zh: 你对这件事不担心，是出于什么直觉？
cues.en: What’s your intuition about it not being your worry?

cues.zh: 本质上是因为还有很多其他事情要操心？
cues.en: Because there’s a lot of other stuff to worry about, essentially?

cues.zh: 你觉得你可能会感到意外吗？
cues.en: You think you could be surprised?

cues.zh: 我们——
cues.en: We-

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: For sure.

cues.zh: ……可能会感到意外？
cues.en: … could be surprised?

cues.zh: 那当然。
cues.en: Of course.

cues.zh: 说它不是我最大的担忧，并不意味着我认为我们不需要去做。
cues.en: Saying it’s not my top worry doesn’t mean I don’t think we need to.

cues.zh: 我认为我们需要在这方面努力。
cues.en: I think we need to work on it.

cues.zh: 这非常难，而我们这里有很优秀的人在从事这项工作。
cues.en: It’s super hard, and we have great people here who do work on that.

cues.zh: 我认为还有很多其他事情我们也必须做对。
cues.en: I think there’s a lot of other things we also have to get right.

cues.zh: 对你来说，目前要跳出框框、连接互联网并不是件容易的事——
cues.en: To you, it’s not super-easy to escape the box at this time, connect to the internet-

cues.zh: 我们之前谈过戏剧性风险。
cues.en: We talked about theatrical risks earlier.

cues.zh: 那就是一种戏剧性风险。
cues.en: That’s a theatrical risk.

cues.zh: 这种事确实可能主导人们看待这个问题的方式。
cues.en: That is a thing that can really take over how people think about this problem.

cues.zh: 而且有一大群非常聪明、我认为非常善意的AI安全研究人员，超级执着于这一个问题，我认为没取得多少进展，但就是超级执着于这一个问题。
cues.en: And there’s a big group of very smart, I think very well-meaning AI safety researchers that got super-hung up on this one problem, I’d argue without much progress, but super-hung up on this one problem.

cues.zh: 其实他们这么做我挺高兴的，因为我觉得我们确实需要多想想这个问题。
cues.en: I’m actually happy that they do that, because I think we do need to think about this more.

cues.zh: 但我觉得它把很多其他非常重要的AI相关风险挤出了讨论空间。
cues.en: But I think it pushed out of the space of discourse a lot of the other very significant AI- related risks.

cues.zh: 我问你一下，你发推不用大写字母的事。
cues.en: Let me ask you about you tweeting with no capitalization.

cues.zh: 你键盘上的Shift键坏了吗？
cues.en: Is the shift key broken on your keyboard?

cues.zh: 为什么有人会在意这个？
cues.en: Why does anyone care about that?

cues.zh: 我非常在意。
cues.en: I deeply care.

cues.zh: 但为什么呢？
cues.en: But why?

cues.zh: 我是说，别人也问过我这个。
cues.en: I mean, other people ask me about that, too.

cues.zh: 有什么直觉吗？
cues.en: Any intuition?

cues.zh: 我觉得原因是一样的。
cues.en: I think it’s the same reason.

cues.zh: 有个诗人，E.E.
cues.en: There’s this poet, E.E.

cues.zh: Cummings，他基本不用大写字母，有点像在对体制说“去你的”。
cues.en: Cummings, that mostly doesn’t use capitalization to say, “Fuck you” to the system kind of thing.

cues.zh: 我觉得人们很多疑，因为他们想让你守规矩。
cues.en: And I think people are very paranoid, because they want you to follow the rules.

cues.zh: 你觉得是这个原因吗？
cues.en: You think that’s what it’s about?

cues.zh: 我觉得是这样的——
cues.en: I think it’s like this-

cues.zh: 就像是，“这家伙不守规矩。”
cues.en: It’s like, “This guy doesn’t follow the rules.

cues.zh: 他不把推文首字母大写。”
cues.en: He doesn’t capitalize his tweets.”

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: “这看起来真的很危险。”
cues.en: “This seems really dangerous.”

cues.zh: “他看起来像个无政府主义者。”
cues.en: “He seems like an anarchist.”

cues.zh: 那不是——
cues.en: That doesn’t-

cues.zh: 你只是在故作诗意吗，潮人？
cues.en: Are you just being poetic, hipster?

cues.zh: 什么是——
cues.en: What’s the-

cues.zh: 我从小是——
cues.en: I grew up as-

cues.zh: 遵守规则，Sam。
cues.en: Follow the rules, Sam.

cues.zh: 我从小就是个重度网瘾少年。
cues.en: I grew up as a very online kid.

cues.zh: 那时候我花大量时间在网上和人聊天，还得用电脑，而且你随时可以退出即时通讯软件。
cues.en: I’d spent a huge amount of time chatting with people back in the days where you did it on a computer, and you could log off instant messenger at some point.

cues.zh: 我在那儿从来不把首字母大写，我觉得大多数互联网小孩都不这么做，或者他们现在还是不这么做。
cues.en: And I never capitalized there, as I think most internet kids didn’t, or maybe they still don’t.

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 其实，我现在是在努力回想，但我觉得首字母大写的用法随着时间越来越少了。
cues.en: And actually, now I’m really trying to reach for something, but I think capitalization has gone down over time.

cues.zh: 如果你读古英语写作，他们会在句子中间把很多随机的词大写，名词之类的，我们现在根本不这么做了。
cues.en: If you read Old English writing, they capitalized a lot of random words in the middle of sentences, nouns and stuff that we just don’t do anymore.

cues.zh: 我个人觉得，把句子开头和某些名字等首字母大写，这规矩挺傻的，但也没关系。
cues.en: I personally think it’s sort of a dumb construct that we capitalize the letter at the beginning of a sentence and of certain names and whatever, but that’s fine.

cues.zh: 而且我以前甚至会给推文首字母大写，因为我想显得专业一点什么的。
cues.en: And then I used to, I think, even capitalize my tweets because I was trying to sound professional or something.

cues.zh: 我已经很久没在私人私信之类的地方用大写字母了。
cues.en: I haven’t capitalized my private DMs or whatever in a long time.

cues.zh: 然后慢慢地，那些更短、更不正式的内容，逐渐越来越接近我跟朋友发短信的方式。
cues.en: And then slowly, stuff like shorter-form, less formal stuff has slowly drifted to closer and closer to how I would text my friends.

cues.zh: 如果我打开一个 Word 文档，在给公司写战略备忘录之类的，我总会用大写。
cues.en: If I pull up a Word document and I’m writing a strategy memo for the company or something, I always capitalize that.

cues.zh: 如果我写一条较长的、更正式的消息，我也总会在那里用大写。
cues.en: If I’m writing a long, more formal message, I always use capitalization there, too.

cues.zh: 所以我仍然记得怎么做。
cues.en: So I still remember how to do it.

cues.zh: 但即便是这一点，也可能逐渐消失。
cues.en: But even that may fade out.

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 但我从没花时间想过这事，所以没有现成的——
cues.en: But I never spend time thinking about this, so I don’t have a ready-made-

cues.zh: 嗯，这挺有意思的。
cues.en: Well, it’s interesting.

cues.zh: 首先，知道 Shift 键没坏是件好事。
cues.en: It’s good to, first of all, know the shift key is not broken.

cues.zh: 它能用。
cues.en: It works.

cues.zh: 我之前主要担心你的——
cues.en: I was mostly concerned about your-

cues.zh: 不，它能用。
cues.en: No, it works.

cues.zh: ……担心你在这方面的情况。
cues.en: … well-being on that front.

cues.zh: 我在想，人们现在还会在 Google 搜索时用大写字母吗。
cues.en: I wonder if people still capitalize their Google searches.

cues.zh: 如果你只是写给自己，或者写 ChatGPT 查询，如果你只是写给自己看，还有人会费心用大写吗？
cues.en: If you’re writing something just to yourself or their ChatGPT queries, if you’re writing something just to yourself, do some people still bother to capitalize?

cues.zh: 大概不会。
cues.en: Probably not.

cues.zh: 不过确实，有一小部分人会，但比例很小。
cues.en: But yeah, there’s a percentage, but it’s a small one.

cues.zh: 会让我这么做的原因是，如果有人说“这是某种……的标志”。因为我肯定能强迫自己用大写字母，这很明显。
cues.en: The thing that would make me do it is if people were like, “It’s a sign of…” Because I’m sure I could force myself to use capital letters, obviously.

cues.zh: 如果这感觉像是对别人的一种尊重之类的，那我就可以去做。
cues.en: If it felt like a sign of respect to people or something, then I could go do it.

cues.zh: 但我不知道。
cues.en: But I don’t know.

cues.zh: 我没想过这个。
cues.en: I don’t think about this.

cues.zh: 我不觉得这是不尊重，只是礼貌的惯例有惯性，然后你会意识到，如果它既不是尊重的表示也不是不尊重的表示，那它对礼貌其实并不重要。
cues.en: I don’t think there’s a disrespect, but I think it’s just the conventions of civility that have a momentum, and then you realize it’s not actually important for civility if it’s not a sign of respect or disrespect.

cues.zh: 但我觉得有一群人，他们只是想让你对此有个明确态度，这样他们就能放下大小写这件事了。
cues.en: But I think there’s a movement of people that just want you to have a philosophy around it so they can let go of this whole capitalization thing.

cues.zh: 我觉得没别人会这么在意这件事。
cues.en: I don’t think anybody else thinks about this as much.

cues.zh: 我是说，也许有些人吧。
cues.en: I mean, maybe some people.

cues.zh: 我认识一些人——
cues.en: I know some people-

cues.zh: 有人每天会想上好几个小时。
cues.en: People think about every day for many hours a day.

cues.zh: 所以我很感激我们把这事说清楚了。
cues.en: So I’m really grateful we clarified it.

cues.zh: 我不可能是唯一一个发推不用大写的人吧。
cues.en: Can’t be the only person that doesn’t capitalize tweets.

cues.zh: 你是唯一一个发推不用大写的公司CEO。
cues.en: You’re the only CEO of a company that doesn’t capitalize tweets.

cues.zh: 我甚至觉得那不是真的，但也许吧。
cues.en: I don’t even think that’s true, but maybe.

cues.zh: 我会非常惊讶。
cues.en: I’d be very surprised.

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 我们会进一步调查，之后再回到这个话题。
cues.en: We’ll investigate further and return to this topic later.

cues.zh: 鉴于Sora能生成模拟世界，让我问你一个脑洞大开的问题。
cues.en: Given Sora’s ability to generate simulated worlds, let me ask you a pothead question.

cues.zh: 这是否增加了你的信念——如果你曾经有过的话——认为我们生活在一个模拟中，也许是由AI系统生成的模拟世界？
cues.en: Does this increase your belief, if you ever had one, that we live in a simulation, maybe a simulated world generated by an AI system?

cues.zh: 有一点。
cues.en: Somewhat.

cues.zh: 我不认为那是最有力的证据。
cues.en: I don’t think that’s the strongest piece of evidence.

cues.zh: 我认为我们能生成世界这一事实，应该多少增加每个人的概率，或者至少稍微提高接受度。
cues.en: I think the fact that we can generate worlds should increase everyone’s probability somewhat, or at least openness to it somewhat.

cues.zh: 但我一直确信我们总有一天能做到像Sora这样的事情。
cues.en: But I was certain we would be able to do something like Sora at some point.

cues.zh: 它比我预想的来得更快，但我想那不算什么大更新。
cues.en: It happened faster than I thought, but I guess that was not a big update.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 但事实上……而且想必它会变得越来越好……你能生成新颖的世界，它们基于训练数据的某些方面，但当你看着它们时，它们是新颖的，这让你想到做这件事有多容易。
cues.en: But the fact that… And presumably, it’ll get better and better and better… You can generate worlds that are novel, they’re based in some aspect of training data, but when you look at them, they’re novel, that makes you think how easy it is to do this thing.

cues.zh: 创造宇宙、打造看似超写实、照片级逼真的完整电子游戏世界，是多么容易。
cues.en: How easy it is to create universes, entire video game worlds that seem ultra-realistic and photo-realistic.

cues.zh: 然后，沉浸在那个世界里又是多么容易，先是借助VR头显，接着是在物理层面。
cues.en: And then how easy is it to get lost in that world, first with a VR headset, and then on the physics-based level?

cues.zh: 最近有人对我说了一番话，我觉得是极其深刻的洞见——有时候会出现一些听起来非常简单、却非常迷幻的洞见。
cues.en: Someone said to me recently, I thought it was a super-profound insight, that there are these very-simple sounding but very psychedelic insights that exist sometimes.

cues.zh: 比如平方根函数，四的平方根，没问题。
cues.en: So the square root function, square root of four, no problem.

cues.zh: 二的平方根，好吧，现在我得琢磨这种新的数了。
cues.en: Square root of two, okay, now I have to think about this new kind of number.

cues.zh: 但一旦我想出平方根函数这个简单概念——你能给孩子讲明白，甚至看看简单几何就能理解它存在——你就可以问：“负一的平方根是什么？”这就是它迷幻的地方。
cues.en: But once I come up with this easy idea of a square root function that you can explain to a child and exists by even looking at some simple geometry, then you can ask the question of “What is the square root of negative one?” And this is why it’s a psychedelic thing.

cues.zh: 这会把你带入另一种完全不同的现实。
cues.en: That tips you into some whole other kind of reality.

cues.zh: 你还能想出很多其他例子，但我认为，卑微的平方根运算符竟能带来如此深刻的洞见和全新的知识领域，这一点在很多方面都适用。
cues.en: And you can come up with lots of other examples, but I think this idea that the lowly square root operator can offer such a profound insight and a new realm of knowledge applies in a lot of ways.

cues.zh: 我认为有很多这样的“运算符”，能解释为什么人们会觉得，他们喜欢的任何版本的模拟假说，可能都比以前以为的更有可能。
cues.en: And I think there are a lot of those operators for why people may think that any version that they like of the simulation hypothesis is maybe more likely than they thought before.

cues.zh: 但对我来说，Sora 能跑通这件事，排不进前五。
cues.en: But for me, the fact that Sora worked is not in the top five.

cues.zh: 我确实认为，广义上讲，AI 在最好的情况下会成为这类入口，简单、迷幻般的入口，通向另一种现实浪潮。
cues.en: I do think, broadly speaking, AI will serve as those kinds of gateways at its best, simple, psychedelic-like gateways to another wave C reality.

cues.zh: 这似乎是确定的。
cues.en: That seems for certain.

cues.zh: 这相当令人兴奋。
cues.en: That’s pretty exciting.

cues.zh: 我以前没试过死藤水，但很快会试。
cues.en: I haven’t done ayahuasca before, but I will soon.

cues.zh: 几周后我要去前面提到的亚马逊丛林。
cues.en: I’m going to the aforementioned Amazon jungle in a few weeks.

cues.zh: 兴奋吗？
cues.en: Excited?

cues.zh: 嗯，我很兴奋。
cues.en: Yeah, I’m excited for it.

cues.zh: 不是死藤水那部分，但那也不错，随便啦。
cues.en: Not the ayahuasca part, but that’s great, whatever.

cues.zh: 但我要在丛林里待几周，深入丛林。
cues.en: But I’m going to spend several weeks in the jungle, deep in the jungle.

cues.zh: 这很令人兴奋，但也很吓人。
cues.en: And it’s exciting, but it’s terrifying.

cues.zh: 我为你感到兴奋。
cues.en: I’m excited for you.

cues.zh: 那里有很多东西能吃掉你、杀死你、毒害你，但那也是自然，是自然的机器。
cues.en: There’s a lot of things that can eat you there, and kill you and poison you, but it’s also nature, and it’s the machine of nature.

cues.zh: 在亚马逊丛林里，你会不由自主地欣赏自然的运作机制。
cues.en: And you can’t help but appreciate the machinery of nature in the Amazon jungle.

cues.zh: 就像这个系统，它就这么存在着，每分每秒、每时每刻都在自我更新。
cues.en: It’s just like this system that just exists and renews itself every second, every minute, every hour.

cues.zh: 它就是那台机器。
cues.en: It’s the machine.

cues.zh: 它让你珍惜我们在这里拥有的东西，人类这个东西是有来源的。
cues.en: It makes you appreciate this thing we have here, this human thing came from somewhere.

cues.zh: 这台进化机器创造了这一切，而在丛林里展现得最为清晰。
cues.en: This evolutionary machine has created that, and it’s most clearly on display in the jungle.

cues.zh: 希望我能活着回来。
cues.en: So hopefully, I’ll make it out alive.

cues.zh: 要是回不来，这就是我们最后一次有趣的对话了，我真的很感激。
cues.en: If not, this will be the last fun conversation we’ve had, so I really deeply appreciate it.

cues.zh: 就像我之前说的，当你仰望星空时，你觉得外面还有其他外星文明吗，那些有智慧的文明？
cues.en: Do you think, as I mentioned before, there’s other alien civilizations out there, intelligent ones, when you look up at the skies?

cues.zh: 我内心深处非常愿意相信答案是肯定的。
cues.en: I deeply want to believe that the answer is yes.

cues.zh: 我觉得费米悖论非常令人费解。
cues.en: I find the Fermi paradox very puzzling.

cues.zh: 让我害怕的是，智慧并不擅长处理——
cues.en: I find it scary that intelligence is not good at handling-

cues.zh: 非常可怕。
cues.en: Very scary.

cues.zh: ……强大的技术。
cues.en: … powerful technologies.

cues.zh: 但与此同时，我相当确信，外面存在着数量极其庞大的智慧外星文明。
cues.en: But at the same time, I think I’m pretty confident that there’s just a very large number of intelligent alien civilizations out there.

cues.zh: 可能只是穿越太空实在太难了。
cues.en: It might just be really difficult to travel through space.

cues.zh: 非常有可能。
cues.en: Very possible.

cues.zh: 这也让我思考智慧的本质。
cues.en: And it also makes me think about the nature of intelligence.

cues.zh: 也许我们对智能的样子真的有盲区，而AI或许能帮我们看清这一点。
cues.en: Maybe we’re really blind to what intelligence looks like, and maybe AI will help us see that.

cues.zh: 这不像智商测试和简单解谜那么简单。
cues.en: It’s not as simple as IQ tests and simple puzzle solving.

cues.zh: 还有更大的东西。
cues.en: There’s something bigger.

cues.zh: 是什么让你对人类未来、我们正在做的这件事、人类文明抱有希望？
cues.en: What gives you hope about the future of humanity, this thing we’ve got going on, this human civilization?

cues.zh: 我觉得过去的分量很重。
cues.en: I think the past is a lot.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，看看人类在并不长的时间里做了什么，巨大的问题、深层的缺陷、很多让人无比羞愧的事。
cues.en: I mean, we just look at what humanity has done in a not very long period of time, huge problems, deep flaws, lots to be super-ashamed of.

cues.zh: 但总体而言，非常鼓舞人心。
cues.en: But on the whole, very inspiring.

cues.zh: 给了我很多希望。
cues.en: Gives me a lot of hope.

cues.zh: 就是这一切的轨迹。
cues.en: Just the trajectory of it all.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我们共同推动着走向更好的未来。
cues.en: That we’re together pushing towards a better future.

cues.zh: 我好奇的一点是，AGI会更像某个单一的大脑，还是更像我们所有人之间社会的脚手架？
cues.en: One thing that I wonder about, is AGI going to be more like some single brain, or is it more like the scaffolding in society between all of us?

cues.zh: 你和你曾曾曾祖父母之间并没有太大的基因漂移，但你的能力却截然不同。
cues.en: You have not had a great deal of genetic drift from your great-great-great grandparents, and yet what you’re capable of is dramatically different.

cues.zh: 你的知识也截然不同。
cues.en: What you know is dramatically different.

cues.zh: 这不是因为生物层面的变化。
cues.en: And that’s not because of biological change.

cues.zh: 我是说，你可能稍微健康了一点。
cues.en: I mean, you got a little bit healthier, probably.

cues.zh: 你有现代医学，吃得更好，诸如此类。
cues.en: You have modern medicine, you eat better, whatever.

cues.zh: 但你拥有的是我们所有人共同搭建的这套脚手架。
cues.en: But what you have is this scaffolding that we all contributed to built on top of.

cues.zh: 没有哪一个人能独自造出 iPhone。
cues.en: No one person is going to go build the iPhone.

cues.zh: 没有哪一个人能独自发现所有科学，但你却可以使用它。
cues.en: No one person is going to go discover all of science, and yet you get to use it.

cues.zh: 这赋予了你不可思议的能力。
cues.en: And that gives you incredible ability.

cues.zh: 所以某种意义上，这一切是我们共同创造的，这让我对未来充满希望。
cues.en: And so in some sense, that we all created that, and that fills me with hope for the future.

cues.zh: 那是一件非常集体性的事情。
cues.en: That was a very collective thing.

cues.zh: 是啊，我们真的是站在巨人的肩膀上。
cues.en: Yeah, we really are standing on the shoulders of giants.

cues.zh: 你提到，我们聊到戏剧化、戏剧性的AI风险时，有时你可能会为自己的生命感到恐惧。
cues.en: You mentioned when we were talking about theatrical, dramatic AI risks that sometimes you might be afraid for your own life.

cues.zh: 你会想到自己的死亡吗？
cues.en: Do you think about your death?

cues.zh: 你会害怕吗？
cues.en: Are you afraid of it?

cues.zh: 我是说，如果我明天中枪了，而我今天就知道，我会想：“哦，那真令人难过。
cues.en: I mean, if I got shot tomorrow and I knew it today, I’d be like, “Oh, that’s sad.

cues.zh: 我想看看会发生什么。
cues.en: I want to see what’s going to happen.

cues.zh: 多么令人好奇的时刻。
cues.en: What a curious time.

cues.zh: 多么有趣的时代。”但我主要只会对自己的人生感到非常感恩。
cues.en: What an interesting time.” But I would mostly just feel very grateful for my life.

cues.zh: 感恩你曾拥有的那些时刻。
cues.en: The moments that you did get.

cues.zh: 是的，我也是。
cues.en: Yeah, me, too.

cues.zh: 这人生相当精彩。
cues.en: It’s a pretty awesome life.

cues.zh: 我能享受人类那些了不起的创造，我相信ChatGPT就是其中之一，还有OpenAI所做的一切。
cues.en: I get to enjoy awesome creations of humans, which I believe ChatGPT is one of, and everything that OpenAI is doing.

cues.zh: Sam，再次和你交谈真是荣幸和愉快。
cues.en: Sam, it’s really an honor and pleasure to talk to you again.

cues.zh: 很高兴和你交谈。
cues.en: Great to talk to you.

cues.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。
cues.en: Thank you for having me.

cues.zh: 感谢收听这次与Sam Altman的对话。
cues.en: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Sam Altman.

cues.zh: 为支持本播客，请查看简介中的赞助商。
cues.en: To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

cues.zh: 现在，让我以 Arthur C.
cues.en: And now let me leave you with some words from Arthur C.

cues.zh: Clarke 的一句话作为结束。
cues.en: Clarke.

cues.zh: “也许我们在这个星球上的角色不是崇拜上帝，而是创造上帝。”感谢收听，希望下次再见。
cues.en: “It may be that our role on this planet is not to worship God, but to create him.” Thank you for listening, and hope to see you next time.
